- **Second source-confirmed defect in the old diagnostics:** XNU's
  `pexpert/gen/bootargs.c:getval()` interprets a leading zero followed by a
  digit as octal. `nord2stopat=0008` is classified as a string, copied into
  the uint32 argument as the first three characters plus NUL, not point 8.
  `0007` and `0005` happened to work. Thus the old stop-8 run is NOT a valid
  after-kperf checkpoint; the successful stop 7 and failed stop 5 still
  bound the failure before BSD. The new test uses **`nord2stopat=8`**.
  The checker now rejects padded decimal stop arguments, and the image
  helper's default is `nord2stopat=2`. The legacy `patch_gate_arg()` in
  `loader.c` also emits padded decimal: do not use automatic `nord2vmstop`
  stepping until that is fixed. It is inactive in the new test image.

- 2026-10-20 (session 8, Codex): **CPU driver matching mismatch found in the
  source; corrected stop 8 now verified above.** This supersedes the final session-7
  explanation below. `ml_wait_max_cpus()` does NOT spin until eight CPUs check
  in: it sleeps on `max_cpus_initialized`, waiting for `ml_set_max_cpus()`.
  `ml_parse_cpu_topology()` honors `cpus=1`; `IODTPlatformExpert::createNubs()`
  only adds `logical-cpu-id` to CPUs selected by that topology. Eight ADT
  nodes therefore do not require eight online CPUs.
  - The real mismatch: Nord 2 CPU nodes had only `arm,cortex-a55/a78` and
    `ARM,v8`, but the only `SweetCPU` personality in `KernelConfigTables.cpp`
    matched `qcom,kryo470`. No Nord 2 CPU could match, and the saved deep-boot
    logs contain no `SWEET CPU:` lines. `SweetCPU::startAll()` normally calls
    `ml_set_max_cpus()` after testing SGI1 on every selected CPU.
  - Fix: add `mediatek,mt6893-cpu` to Nord 2 CPU compatible lists and a separate
    `SweetCPU` personality for that token (patch 0082). Keep the actual Cortex
    types, Sweet's existing Qualcomm match, `cpus=1`, and the normal kperf wait.
    `tools/nord2-mkpatch.sh` now includes `iokit/KernelConfigTables.cpp`.
    Build with Apple clang via CI; do not use fake `__builtin_xnu_*` fallbacks.
  - Next test: CI kernel + new ADT, `nord2stopat=8` (after kperf, before
    `bsd_init`). Expected evidence: `SWEET CPU: requested=1 selected=1`,
    `1/1 CPUs initialized, SGI1 verified`, stop 8, chain-back to Android.
    A failure may expose a further CPU/GIC issue; do not claim a working fix
    until the log proves it. Do not try `cpus=8` as a workaround or skip kperf.

    full boot partition SHA-256

- 2026-10-19 (session 6, Claude): **root cause of the silence after
  `SWEET BATTERY` identified in the source (not yet tested on the phone).**
  `pmap_switch_user_ttb()` (osfmk/arm/pmap/pmap.c:7577-7587) loads
  `invalid_ttep` into TTBR0 when it switches to a kernel thread, so the
  bootstrap V=P map that the console used (pmsg 0x48160000, framebuffer
  0x76e10000, DSI/MUTEX MMIO) disappears with the first context switch — that is
  when the log stopped. It also explains why the late stop at the end of
  `arm_init` worked (no switch yet). The bootstrap table itself is NOT reused:
  `bootstrap_pagetables` is read-only-late data and `cpu.c:928-935` cleans it to
  PoC to start secondary CPUs, so it stays a valid V=P table for the whole boot
  (the earlier "XNU reuses the bootstrap tables" note was wrong).
  Fix (patch 0082): `nord2_console_remap()` right after `arm_vm_init()` maps
  pmsg and framebuffer with `ml_io_map_wcomb` and DSI0/DISP_MUTEX with
  `ml_io_map` (TTBR1 aliases, valid in every thread); `nord2_phys()` and the
  frame push use them. `nord2_leave_to()` now masks DAIF first, uses the cached
  chain-back values before any device-tree lookup, and reloads TTBR0 with
  `kvtophys(bootstrap_pagetables)` + TLB flush before the trampoline
  (verified in the linked kernel's disassembly). Expected on screen after the
  test: `console remapped to kernel VA`, then the log continues past the
  battery line to the real failure, or to hook 2 and back to Android.
  - New `tools/nord2-mkpatch.sh`: regenerates 0082 from the buildtree and checks
    it applies to the pristine CI sources and reproduces the buildtree.
  - Images rebuilt (all `FAILURES: none`, 30.568.448 bytes). Test candidate
    `nord2-xnu-late2.img` SHA-256

    (`nord2stopat=0002`, on-screen log). Previous outputs moved to
    `shim/out/nord2-xnu.prev-*`.

  - **Root cause of the logo hang (a loader bug, not LK):** `same()` compares
    up to a NUL, but `payload.magic` is 8 bytes *not* NUL-terminated and is
    followed by `version = 1`, so `same(pl->magic, "SWEETXNU")` returned false
    always → `fatal("no SWEETXNU payload")` → the old fatal spun in `wfe`
    (first flash) / chained back (second flash). Fixed with a fixed-width
    `magic8()` comparison. The ADT property-name uses of `same()` are fine
    (32-byte NUL-padded fields).

  **`arm_vm_init` HANGS** (no panic): Android never came back, the user saw a

  - The loader now *preserves* an existing ring instead of resetting it
    (`previous log preserved` line), and **DRAM does survive a normal
    reboot** — after `adb reboot` the file held the earlier Android pmsg data
    plus both probe runs (`backup/nord2/probe-v8-reboot-pmsg.txt`, 2158
    bytes). But **DRAM does not survive the reset that follows a hang**
    (cold/WDT): at the next boot the loader found no previous ring, so the
    hung run's log is unrecoverable. Any future step that can hang must
    therefore be *bounded by a stop hook that returns to Android*, never run
    to a hang.
  - Note: `/sys/fs/pstore/pmsg-ramoops-0` is a *shared* zone — Android writes
    its own "TENS" records into it through `/dev/pmsg0`, so the file contains
    Android records followed by our appended probe log.
  - Next plan (agreed shape): instrument `arm_vm_init` with a sequence of
    numbered gates (`nord2_vm_gate(stage)`, controlled by a boot argument)
    that each log `NORD2-NEXT=<stage+1>` and chain back to Android; the
    loader reads that value out of the preserved previous log and rewrites
    the `nord2vmstop=` field of the payload command line in RAM before XNU
    starts. One flash, then each plain reboot advances the gate by one step
    until a boot hangs: the last `NORD2-NEXT` seen is the failing step.
    Rebuild images (30.562.304 bytes, all verified):

    after `pmap_bootstrap`, after the early I/O tables, and at the end). A gate
    stops only when `stage >= nord2vmstop` and logs
    `NORD2-XNU: gate 0x… stop; NORD2-NEXT=0x…`. The loader scans the
    *preserved* ring for the last `NORD2-NEXT=0x…` and rewrites the four
    digits after `nord2vmstop=` in the payload command line (in RAM, before
    `boot_args` are filled) — so one image walks one gate per reboot. Images:
    `nord2-xnu-vmstep.img`
    `4e943109a6824ff19d4bd1b9f0842318bea4ff24c897080d0c126983fe6ef3b8`

**Phone workflow (user does buttons, Claude runs commands):**
- Boot test kernel: phone in fastboot -> `fastboot boot shim/out/shim-boot-X.img`. NEVER `fastboot getvar`.
- **Read logs WITHOUT filming:** after a test the user holds Power+VolDown -> fastboot -> `fastboot boot recovery/recovery.img` (OrangeFox, temp) -> wait for `adb shell true` -> `tools/sweet-log-pull.sh user@host/android/ios-sweet-work/logs/<name>.txt` (reads the 4 MiB console ring the kernel keeps in the last 1025 blocks of userdata; patch 0047). Then `adb reboot bootloader` brings the phone back to fastboot without the user.
- **Flash a root image:** `fastboot flash -S 512M userdata <img>.simg` (7 min, 25 chunks). After a big flash the Xiaomi ABL fastboot hangs: next `fastboot boot` stalls at "Sending" -> the USER must re-enter fastboot by hand (Power+VolDown). Do not retry commands against the hung ABL. A flash right after `adb reboot bootloader` once failed on chunk 1 (USB protocol error): just retry. User must NOT unplug during flash (once interrupted at 25/25 -> reflash).
- **Edit the phone root without reflashing (same-length only):** find the file's raw offset in the local image (it is one extent; search the image for its first 4 KiB), compare with `adb exec-out dd if=/dev/block/sda34 ...`, then `adb push` changed 4 KiB blocks and `dd of=/dev/block/sda34 seek=... conv=notrunc,fsync`, read back. Recovery kernel has no hfsplus.
- **Pull the whole phone root** (12 min): `adb exec-out "dd if=/dev/block/sda34 bs=1048576 count=16384" > img`; mount ro with udisksctl or `sudo mount -t hfsplus -o loop,ro`. To write into a pulled image: `sudo fsck.hfsplus -fy` first (volume is never cleanly unmounted -> Linux mounts ro even with -o force), then `sudo mount -t hfsplus -o loop,force`.
- Making images: copy latest img with `cp --sparse=always`, mount rw with force, change, `sync; umount`, `sha256sum`, `img2simg`. Keep only the latest image + one fallback on the SSD (/home is ~98% full; big work files live in `user@host/android/ios-sweet-work/`, old kernels/images archived in `.../ios-sweet-work/archive/`).

- **IOMobileFramebuffer swap + notification ABI (2026-10-17, offline).** Swap record = fb+0x18, **0x46c bytes**, zeroed by SwapBegin and sent whole by `kern_SwapEnd` = IOConnectCallStructMethod(sel 5, rec, 0x46c, no output). **SwapBegin** = sel 4, no input, 1 scalar out = swap id (stored at rec+0x50). `kern_SwapSetLayer(fb, layer<4, IOSurfaceRef, CGRect a, CGRect b, flags)`: rec+0x54+4*layer = **IOSurface id**; rec+0x104 bit layer = layer enabled (rec+0x108 bit cleared); rect a (int x,y,w,h, scaled) at rec+0x64+16*layer, rect b at rec+0xc4+16*layer; rec+0x114+4*layer = transform from flags&0xf; flag bits 5/31/6/7/8/9 set bytes rec+0x2ca/0x2cc/0x2e3/0x2e5/0x2e6/0x467+layer. A NULL surface only sets the enable bit with zero id. SwapWait = sel 6 scalars [swap id, timeout, 0].
  - **Notifications**: `IOMobileFramebufferScheduleWithDispatchQueue`/`GetRunLoopSource` create an IONotificationPort and `IOConnectSetNotificationPort(conn, type, port, 0)` (kernel `registerNotificationPort`). `kern_EnableNotifications(fb, type, cb, ctx)` = **sel 72 scalars [NotifyCallbackFuncs[type], fb, type, 0]** -> the kernel keeps an async reference {port, func, refcon=fb} per type and fires it with `sendAsyncResult64`. Types: 0 HotPlug, 1 Power, 3 FrameInfo (args[0] = mask of 31-bit keys, args[1] u32, then values), 4 CRC, **5 Vsync**: 6 args, each a 32-bit half in a u64 slot: (ts lo, ts hi), (t2 lo, hi) passed through the time-ingest helper, (t3 lo, hi); the framework then calls the client's vsync callback(fb, ts, t2', t3, ctx). Vsync callbacks are dropped while the notification port has queued messages.

LookupFromMachPort = sel 0x22 (scalar in [port name]); CreateMachPort = sel 0x23 (scalar in [id, options], scalar out [port name]).
  - Lock result (copied to client+0x68, size 0x68 + planes*0x80, min 0xe8): 0x00 u64 base address **mapped in the caller's task**; 0x08 u64 task VA of a per-surface shared state page (+0 u64 registry id, +8/+0xa u16 bound accel ids, +0xc u32 seed, +0x14 u8 tiled, +0x20 u32 value generation, +0x24 YCbCr matrix, +0x28 u32 non-bulk values size, +0x2d u8 displayable, +0x2e u8 sysmem-only, +0x30 0x70 bytes bulk attachments); 0x10 u64 task VA of timestamp page (4 u64 indexed timestamps, +0x20 detach code); 0x18 u32 surface id; 0x1c u32 alloc size; 0x20 width; 0x24 height; 0x28 bytes per row; 0x2c buffer offset; 0x30 pixel format; 0x34 u32 (dcache flush length); 0x38 plane count; 0x40 u16 bytes/element; 0x42 u8 element width; 0x43 u8 element height; 0x44 cache mode; 0x4c u8 subsampling; 0x4d u8 prohibit-use count; 0x50 parent id; 0x54 slice count; 0x58 u64 trace id; 0x60 u64 protection options; planes[n] at 0x68+n*0x80 (+0 width, +4 height, +8 bytes/row, +0xc offset, +0x14 size, +0x18 u16 bpe, +0x1a/+0x1b u8 element w/h, +0x1c u8 component count, +0x1d address format, +0x54 u8 compression type (non-zero -> no CPU base address)).

- Faulting instruction: `ldr x0, [x8, #0x150]` in crypto_random_kmem_ctx_size; x8 = NULL g_crypto_funcs. Source: libkern/crypto/corecrypto_rand.c and osfmk/vm/vm_kern.c:2448. rand.h explicitly permits NON-cryptographic kmem RNGs, but requires no locking in generation and context size <=256. Do not substitute read_random here: the global PRNG provider is also unregistered and kmem generation must remain lock-free. early_random may seed contexts during single-CPU bootstrap; it uses the built-in HMAC-SHA256 DRBG with the host-generated ADT seed.
- Patch 0013 keeps the replacement entirely private to vm_kern.c: SplitMix64 state is 8 bytes per CPU/sizeclass, initialized using early_random. Uniform selection uses rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias. Other platforms retain the original corecrypto calls; SWEET's generic crypto APIs/registration remain untouched. Reference: https://prng.di.unimi.it/splitmix64.c (Sebastiano Vigna, public domain).

## QEMU emulation (2026-10-15)
- `tools/mkadt.py OUT.adt --qemu` = same ADT with QEMU virt GICD 0x08000000 / GICR 0x080a0000 / CNTFRQ 62.5 MHz.
- `tools/qemu-sweet.py PAYLOAD OUTDIR [--secs N] [--hmp "x /8gx ADDR"] [--gdb]`: host-side copy of shim/loader.c
  (segments + ADT + boot_args at their PAs, 6-instruction stub sets x0 and jumps), `-M virt,gic-version=3 -cpu cortex-a76`
  (same ID_AA64MMFR0 as Kryo 470), 4G RAM so 0x9c000000 fb and 0xb0000000 kernel are plain RAM.
  Outputs `fb.png` (the screen), `regs.txt`, `qemu.log` (exceptions with ESR/FAR/ELR). `--gdb` halts with a stub on :1234
  (system `gdb` + `set architecture aarch64`, `hbreak *VA` works with the MMU on).
- Not emulated: Qualcomm XPUs, ABL, real panel, PSCI conduit (QEMU virt uses hvc). Hardware still decides those.
- Example: `python3 tools/mkadt.py /tmp/q.adt --qemu && python3 tools/mkpayload.py xnu/out-0013/kernel.development.sweet /tmp/q.adt /tmp/pq.bin --cmdline 'debug=0xc serial=3 cpus=1 keepsyms=1 -enable_kprintf_spam' && python3 tools/qemu-sweet.py /tmp/pq.bin /tmp/q`

## Layout
- `backup/`  partition dumps + full sdb..sdf LUNs, `SHA256SUMS` (all verified on-device == local)
- `dtb/`     live FDT (from OrangeFox), PixelOS boot.img dtb, dtbo, dts versions
- `shim/`    bare-metal boot shim (`./build.sh` -> `out/shim-boot.img`)
- `research/` mainline sm7150 dts, XNU pe_fiq.c etc, PocketDarwin patches
- `tools/unpack_bootv2.py`

## Device access
- No root in PixelOS 17 (user build, adb root disabled). Root = `fastboot boot recovery/recovery.img` (OrangeFox R12.0_2, temp boot, not flashed).
- `fastboot boot` works for stock boot.img, OrangeFox, and our shim.
- Shim resets itself via PSCI SYSTEM_RESET; IMEM restart_reason 0x77665500 is seen
  (bootreason=bootloader) but ABL still boots Android, so it does not stop in fastboot.

## Hardware facts (live DT + shim measurements)
- Framebuffer (ABL cont splash): 0x9c000000, 1080x2400, stride 4320, a8r8g8b8, panel is DSC *video* mode (no kick needed).
- RAM: 0x80000000+2G, 0x100000000+0xfcc00000. Live reserved-memory = PixelOS base dtb + sweet dtbo fixups.
- GICv3: GICD 0x17a00000, GICR 0x17a60000 (stride 0x20000, 8 PEs). GICD_TYPER 0x007B041D: SecurityExtn=1 (DS=0).
  ABL leaves GICD_CTLR = 0x10 (ARE_NS on, groups off). Writing 0x13 reads back 0x12: EnableGrp1A (bit1) is the one that matters.
- GIC Group 1 VERIFIED (shim 2c): vtimer INTID 19 = 30 IRQs/300ms, ptimer INTID 18 = 30, SGI 1 to self = 10/10.
  ICC_SRE=1 already, ICC_CTLR 0x8440, priority/enable writes stick. GICR_IGROUPR0 and GICD_IGROUPRn read 0 from NS
  even though Group 1 delivery works (RAZ in NS view) - do not use them as a health check.
  INTID 28 shows pending constantly (unknown PPI 12).
- Timer 19.2 MHz. Qualcomm PPI numbering: secure-phys/phys/virt/hyp = PPI 1/2/3/0 -> vtimer INTID 19, ptimer 18 (NOT 27/30).
- PSCI 1.1 via SMC, SMCCC 1.1. CPU_ON ok; SYSTEM_SUSPEND and SYSTEM_RESET2 unsupported.
- SMP: CPU_ON works for all 7 secondaries (MPIDR 0x81000n00).
- Entry EL1, MMU off, x0 = DTB (magic ok). ID_AA64MMFR0 = ...101122: 16K granule YES, 4K YES.
- No serial console: debug UART SE is in SPI mode on sweet. Screen is the only debug channel.

## XNU implications
- XNU GICv3 path (pexpert/arm/pe_fiq.c, VMAPPLE) puts the timer (PPI 27) in Group 0 = FIQ. With SecurityExtn=1,
  Group 0 is secure -> impossible from NS EL1. Need: Group 1 IRQ, ICC_IGRPEN1, INTID 19, and the timer handled in the IRQ path.
- XNU VMAPPLE PSCI uses `hvc`; sweet needs `smc`.
- PocketDarwin NonAppleGenericCpu.patch only swaps -mcpu=apple-h7 for -march=armv8-a.

## Milestone 3 (2026-10-14): 16K MMU verified
- ABL loads the Image at 0x80080000 (base 0x80000000 + 0x80000) regardless of text_offset=0.
- 16K granule, T0SZ=28 (L2 start, 32MB blocks), MAIR 0x44ff00, TCR 0x1409CB51C, PARange=2 (40-bit PA).
- Only own image pages WB (Qualcomm XPUs: never map carve-outs cacheable); fb Normal-NC; rest Device.
- AT S1E1R checks all as expected; unmapped -> translation fault L2.
- Fill fb: 110 ms (MMU off) -> 3.5 ms (NC). Memory loop 70 ms -> 0.7 ms. vtimer + SGI IRQs still fine with MMU on.

## XNU loader design notes (xnu-8796)
- Entry: `_start` -> `start_first_cpu`, x0 = boot_args (PA), MMU off, EL1. boot_args: Revision/Version 2,
  virtBase/physBase/memSize/topOfKernelData, Boot_Video (fb 0x9c000000, rowBytes 4320, 1080x2400, depth 32),
  deviceTreeP/Length (ADT), CommandLine[608], bootFlags, memSizeActual.
- start.s maps [kernel mach header .. physBase+memSize) with cacheable BLOCKS. On Qualcomm every XPU carve-out
  must therefore lie below the kernel: use physBase = 0xb0000000 (above ramdump_fb 0xaf000000+16M,
  cdsp_sec, qseecom), end before rmtfs 0xfde01000 -> memSize ~0x4d000000 for bring-up.
- Base ADT: iPhone 8 d20ap DeviceTree from iOS 16.7.16 IPSW (tools/remotezip.py + tools/adt.py; LZFSE payload).
  Template values are empty: the loader must fill chosen/*, memory-map, cpu*/reg etc. like iBoot.
- XNU build: GitHub Actions (dipa-studio/ios-sweet, xnu.yml) via blacktop/darwin-xnu-build, MACOS_VERSION=13.5.
  New-clang fixes in xnu/patches; Xcode 16 iig is incompatible (IORPC.kernelContent) -> macos-14 runner, oldest Xcode.

## Kernel architecture plan (SWEET machine config)
- First stock build (VMAPPLE) is arm64e (PAC). Kryo 470 = ARMv8.2, no PAC -> SWEET must build plain arm64
  (HAS_APPLE_PAC is only defined for __arm64e__, so arm64 drops PAC automatically).
- Template: VMAPPLE (16K pages, GICv3 code in pe_fiq.c) minus APPLEVIRTUALPLATFORM hypercalls/paravirt PAC,
  plus BCM2837 (generic ARM: no APPLE_ARM64_ARCH_FAMILY Apple sysregs). Do not link the KDK lib<cfg>.os.*.a.
- Timer: XNU expects it on FIQ (sleh_fiq -> rtclock_intr). SWEET: GIC Group 1, so sleh_irq must ack ICC_IAR1,
  route INTID 19 to the same timer path, SGIs to cpu_signal_handler, EOI via ICC_EOIR1.
- SMP/interrupts: open-source AppleARMSMP (USE_APPLEARMSMP) needs an IOInterruptController (AIC role) and an
  IOPMGR (CPU power -> PSCI CPU_ON via SMC). Plan: built-in IOKit classes (SweetGIC, SweetPMGR, platform
  expert) compiled into the kernel and matched via iokit/KernelConfigTables.cpp -> no closed kexts needed.
- Debug: xnu patch 0003 sweet-fbcon = kprintf drawn on the framebuffer (ADT node "sweet-fbcon").
- ADT /arm-io ranges must not map to parent 0 (pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys()==0 disables serial): use parent 0x1000000.

- 2026-10-19 (session 7, Opencode): **ROOT CAUSE of the reset: the toprgu pet was
  writing the wrong register.** The MediaTek toprgu layout (vendor
  `aee/hangdet/aee_hangdet.c` and `watchdog/mtk_wdt.c`) is
  `WDT_MODE = 0x00` (bit0 = enable), `WDT_LENGTH = 0x04`,
  **`WDT_RST = 0x08` with magic `0x1971`**, `WDT_STATUS = 0x0c`. Our code wrote
  `0x1971` to **0x04 (LENGTH)** and read "status"/"interval" at 0x08/0x0c, so
  the AP watchdog was **never kicked** — and the Nord 2 DT enables the MT6360
  AP-watchdog reset input (`apwdtrst_en = <1>`, MT6360 on I2C, not pwrap).
  That explains every observation: `wdt_mode = 0x7d` (enabled), `wdt_length`
  read from the wrong register showed 0, petting had no effect, the reset is
  time-based and independent of the log, and `bootreason = PMIC_cold_reboot`.
  Fix: kick `WDT_RST` (offset 0x08) and log `MODE/LENGTH/STATUS` from their
  real offsets. Image `nord2-xnu-late2.img` 30.568.448 bytes SHA-256

    `kperf_init_early()` is the stall.
  - Source (`osfmk/kperf/kperf.c:77`): `kperf_init_early()` starts with
    `ml_wait_max_cpus();` — it **spins until `machine_info.max_cpus` CPUs have
    checked in**. Our ADT advertises **8 CPU nodes** and the probe boots with
    `cpus=1` (only CPU0 online), so the wait never completes: that is the
    silent, timer-starving stall right after the IOKit matching, and the AP
    watchdog (`WDT_RST` now correctly kicked, ~10 s timeout) resets the SoC
    with `PMIC_cold_reboot`.

## 2026-11-11 night: FIRST HARDWARE H.264 ENCODE ON THE PHONE (MT6893 VENC)

Result (run vc14, kernel q10je, payload vc2-encode: vcodecd c5e750bb, probe c24a6a1b, vendor set = the phone's own five Android objects hosted under our AArch32 interpreter in `vcodecd` on iOS 16.7): `N2VCDP DONE ok=1 frames=10/10 keys=1 bytes=19367 hw_ms=73`; the stream `probe-43.h264` (kept in `gpu/build/apps-20261104/vcodec-fetch/vc14/out/`) is H.264 Baseline 640x480, 10 frames, decodes with `ffmpeg -xerror` with no error and the first frame is the test pattern. Kernel log: `venc_sel 0xc030601 -> 0x4030601 (273 MHz)`, `first VENC done status 0x4`, `first VENC_C1 done status 0x4`. Per frame hardware time about 7.2 ms at 640x480 (rtt 7 ms). Not proved: 1080p, frame rate, rate control quality, HEVC on the phone, decode, VideoToolbox/Camera use (plug-in has the hardware encoders OFF behind /var/db/nord2-video-claim-hw).
Bugs found on the way (all fixed): iOS 16 KiB pages vs 4 KiB `mprotect` in the guest memory; jetsam per-process limit (6 MB effective) killing vcodecd -> `memorystatus_control` raises to 3072 MB; ION flags forwarded to RWVC_DMA_ALLOC (kernel EINVAL) -> flags 0; kernel relay `/dev/redwood-vcodec-client` held a `proc_find` reference in the slot until close (phone reset about 0.5 s after the probe's open) -> client = pid+uniqueid, no reference (q10je); the daemon-side debug trace delays (kern.n2vctrace, 2 s per ioctl) must be switched off (probe sets it 0).
Images: q10jy (full series, no VCT trace) is NOT usable with the relay bug; q10je = q10jy + relay fix + VCT trace (4096 B boot spare). TODO: rebuild the final image without the trace delays (keep the relay fix), then decode/VideoToolbox/mic/I2C checks. Sources: `gpu/hwcodec/` (PLAN.md, FIRST_PHONE_TEST.md, CRITICAL_PATH.md, facts/*.md), patches `gpu/hwcodec/kern/p031x`, `gpu/build/audio-capture-20261111`, `gpu/build/i2c8cam-20261111`. Phone control scripts: `gpu/build/autocycle/txn.sh`, `gpu/build/apps-20261104/{stage-vcodec.sh,vcodec_check.py,rehearse-vcodec.sh}`.
- 1080p H.264 hardware encode on the phone (run vc16, q10je, VENC clock 273 MHz): 30/30 frames 1920x1080 (buffer 1920x1088), 8 Mbit/s requested, 982042 B stream (about 7.9 Mbit/s over the 30 frames), Baseline, decodes with ffmpeg without error; hardware time 29.4-29.5 ms per frame (hw_us), OPEN (INIT) 51 ms. At 273 MHz that is just inside 30 fps; 4K would need the 624 MHz clock or both cores (not tested).

## 2026-11-12T03:59:04+01:00 — analisi Fable jp4: il decoder JPEG PARTE (ipotesi precedente errata)

Causa probabile: registro 0x344 programmato con indice MCU, ma per Linux upstream e' la DIMENSIONE DEL BITSTREAM in byte (JPGDEC_REG_BIT_STREAM_SIZE); manca anche DU_NUM 0x0FC nel set 2015. ## 2026-11-12T04:07:39+01:00 — causa codifica JPEG HW (analisi Fable su jp5)
Non fallisce tutto: 7 codifiche su 13 passano (640x480 q97/95/60, 1080p q95/60, 12MP q95 in 28.5 ms, 2592x1944 q90); le 6 che falliscono hanno tutte 'NORD2 JPEG: no FF D9 in the last 64 bytes of N' (RWJ_E_SIZE). Il blocco arrotonda a 128 byte, non 64: padding dopo EOI 0..127, n2jd_cut() guarda solo gli ultimi 64 (nord2_jpegdev.inc:328-338). Hardware finito regolarmente. Fix: ricerca in avanti di FF D9 dagli ultimi 256 byte -> patch 0317, kernel q10jk (Opus a3f7350a in costruzione). Indipendente da 0316 e dal layout pool.

## 2026-11-12T06:22:26+01:00 — ANALISI dp1: il decoder HW dei plug-in prod3/prod4 e' ROTTO a ogni dimensione (non e' un limite 176x144) — IMPORTANTE per la build unica
Causa verificata sul PC con gli oggetti vendor sotto decint: il plug-in invia DEC_HEADER con solo SPS/PPS (n2vtd_obj.c:419) e poi i frame senza; il vendor non conserva un header senza slice -> H.264: sessione HW aperta ma 0 immagini, nessun errore (statuses 0, frames 8/8 'droppati', md5 none; 1080p con B-frame idem 0/10); HEVC: un header senza slice fallisce sempre (eVDecDrvInit fail (6) -> -12911 'DEC_HEADER/pool refused'), il fallback software di prod4 funziona. Con SPS/PPS davanti al primo frame: H.264 176x144 8/8, 1080p 10/10. 'daemon busy -12913' = artefatto della sonda (decoder aperto mentre l'encoder tiene l'unica sessione di vcodecd), non un leak; la CLOSE dopo StartSession fallita funziona. CONSEGUENZA: con prod3/prod4 un filmato H.264 (anche quelli della Camera, 1080p) in Photos prenderebbe la sessione HW e mostrerebbe NIENTE. Il decoder del prod3 attuale NON va consegnato: usare payload-vcodec-prod5 (fix: prepend_params(), SPS/PPS in testa al primo frame e a ogni keyframe senza SPS; HEVC resta sul fallback software; host test DEC06 2952/2952) oppure, se prod5 non regge sul telefono, payload-vcodec-prod3-nohwdec (encode hw, decode software). dp3 (prod5-probe) in coda per la prova. decode_probe_check.py corretto (conta N2VDEC di ogni processo).

# RAPPORTO COMPLETO (notte 11-12 nov 2026) — codec hardware MediaTek su Nord2 / iOS 16.7

## Cosa funziona, VERIFICATO SUL TELEFONO (numeri)
Codifica (VENC, daemon vcodecd con librerie vendor in interprete AArch32):
- H.264 e HEVC fino a 4K (3840x2160) e 1080p60. HEVC 4K 47.8 ms/frame a 273 MHz (17.9 fps, 3.9 MB); HEVC 4096x2176; riapertura HEVC nello stesso processo OK (vc27: 1080p 30/30 in 766 ms, 4K 30/30 in 1426 ms, 1080p60 60/60 in 1553 ms) dopo il fix heap-zero; switch di clock a 624 MHz funzionante.
- Camera, registrazione video 1080p30 H.264 High sul VENC con zero errori: cam2 (q10ji) 1263 immagini in 42 s = 30.0 fps, 80.8 MB; cam3/cam5 (q10jk, prod3/prod4) 27.4-27.5 fps; cam6 (q10jk + prod5) 418 immagini, 27.6 fps, 14.1 Mbit/s; filmati controllati sul PC (1 slice/picture = VENC, ffmpeg decode OK, audio AAC -47 dB non silenzioso). Baseline software: 21 fps. Il cap a ~27-30 fps e' del sensore/scena; il VENC regge ~30 ms/immagine.
Decodifica (VDEC):
- H.264 e HEVC bit-exact fino a 4K / 4096x2176 con il client standalone (hash per immagine vs ffmpeg); con pipeline a 4 thread (dec4k2): HEVC 1080p60 ~90 fps, HEVC 4K ~74 fps (senza hash), H.264/HEVC altre coppie 39-84 fps.
- VP8/VP9/AV1 bit-exact 10/10; MPEG-2 (68.6 dB), MPEG-4 (57.4 dB), H.263 (58.4 dB) vs ffmpeg = corretti (solo arrotondamento IDCT).
- Via VideoToolbox (plug-in Slim.videodecoder prod6, sonda n2vt_probe, 176x144): H.264 E HEVC su hardware, md5 match 8/8 (dp4); HEVC con DEC_HEADER differito al primo IRAP.
JPEG (VEN condiviso, /dev/redwood-jpeg, kernel q10jk):
- Codifica: 11/11 dimensioni ok (jp7): 1080p q90 258.7 KB hw 4.66 ms (172.9 fps nel bench), 12 MP 27.0-27.3 ms hw (30.7 fps), ~2.2 ms/MP.
- Decodifica: ok a tutte le dimensioni (jp8, passo F5): 640x480 75 dB vs libjpeg, 1080p 4:2:2 con restart 76.6 dB hw 4.7 ms, 12 MP 77.1 dB hw 19.8 ms (~1.6 ms/MP), max|diff|=1.
Altro: microfono presente nei filmati (cam6/cam3 audio ok); HEIC: ImageIO scrive a TILE 512x512 (hm1-heic).

## Cosa NON e' fatto / NON provato (onesto)
- Playback di un filmato in Photos con il decoder hardware: NON esercitato a mano (solo sonda 176x144). Miniature nella griglia ancora assenti.
- Decode 1080p/4K reale VIA VideoToolbox (non standalone): non provato; seek con GOP aperto non provati.
- Nessun percorso di produzione per JPEG o HEIC hardware nella Camera/CMPhoto: le foto restano software (solo design in JPEG_INTEGRATION.md / HEIC_HW_PLAN.md; HEIC hw richiede percorso a tile).
- Foto HEIC con mosaico di tile sfasati nel visore Photos: bug preesistente, non causato dal nostro decoder (nessuna attivita' N2VDEC); da indagare.
- Fallback software DURANTE una registrazione gia' iniziata: assente (un guasto del daemon la termina con errore). All'avvio il fallback c'e' (encoder via VT, decoder in-oggetto).
- 4K30 Camera, VC-1/MT2T/P010 10-bit: non fatto (possibile blocco eFuse sul 10 bit).
- vt17 (diagnostico Photos) e still4096 mai installati; il passo kernel/audio (bundle 1aea9991 nel boot image) e' provato solo come parte delle run camera.
- IRQ reale VENC non usato (polling adattivo); gestione DVFSRC/vcore nel kernel assente; boot spare 2048 B.

## Come eseguire / provare (tutto in gpu/hwcodec/BIG_BUILD.md)
Build unica = 3 transazioni con il kernel q10jk (sha 36aca6cf8bddd242): (1) vt17, (2) still4096, (3) payload-vcodec-prod6 (vcodecd 8fbbd9ab, encoder 91bd53af, decoder 9f23d1e5). Comandi: cd gpu/build; bash big_build_chain.sh --check (deve finire PREFLIGHT_OK); bash big_build_chain.sh big1 (~45 min; START_AT=still4096|vcodec; VCODEC_PAYLOAD=prod5 oppure prod5-nohwdec come ripiego). Telefono in fastboot all'inizio. Dopo l'avvio: Camera > Video, registrare; verifica: python3 gpu/hwcodec/cam/cam_check.py log LIVE.log (atteso hw_encoder_used=yes software_fallbacks=0) e fetch_media.sh + cam_check.py movie.
Ripiego completo: kernel q10ji a1098364 (camera video provato), q10iu a7640bf5 (recovery); undo payload per passo.

gpu/hwcodec/HARDWARE_CODECS.md (architettura, bug B1-B17, sezioni 7-8 decoder), BIG_BUILD.md, CAMERA_INTEGRATION.md, JPEG_PHONE_TEST.md, HEIC_HW_PLAN.md, kern/p031x/STATUS.md (patch 0316 ioctl JPEG, 0317 EOI trim), gpu/build/big_build_chain.sh, payload in gpu/build/apps-20261104/payload-vcodec-prod5/prod6/prod5-nohwdec, kernel gpu/build/device-mmu-q10jk-candidate/, tool gpu/hwcodec/cam/{cam_check,decode_probe_check}.py, jpeg/phone/phone_report.py.

- Symptom (measured by coordinator on IMG_0065.MOV, 1080p30, desk lamp, camera moved a bit): luma 48..133, a new level every 3-4 frames, steps +-30-50 %, period ~20-25 frames (0.7 s); in the file (capture AE), not display. - Root cause (code VERIFIED, effect reproduced in host sim, phone confirmation pending):
  1. stale statistics: rwcam_core.c gs_take() gives AE the GPU stats of a frame 1-3 frames older (made after AE ran on that frame), paired with the NEWEST frame's header; camera_isp.c isp_ae() then thinks the levels are "settled" (header==asked + ISP_AE_SETTLE=2) while they were taken with the old exposure -> corrects the same error twice -> staircase overshoot. Became active with GPU stats (libmerge5/6: "exposure statistics by the GPU for 294 of 301 frames").
  2. highlights rule all-or-nothing (camera_isp.c:241-246 old): brightest 1 % >= 0.95 white -> target x0.5 at once, else full target -> a lamp ~1 % of the picture (camera moving) toggles exposure x2/x0.5. Even with fresh stats this alone gives luma range ~43, jumps ~30 in sim.

## 2026-11-12 ~20:30 GNSS M3 engine on iOS: runtime decided (host analysis; details gpu/hwcodec/GNSS_ENGINE.md section 5)
- libmnl.so exists only as AArch64 (vendor/lib64/mt6893; no 32-bit copy) -> the vcodecd A32 interpreter does not apply and is not needed: run it NATIVELY. Verified clean: 0 x18, 0 svc, 0 tpidr (no TLS), 0 exclusive/LSE atomics, no TEXTREL/INIT_ARRAY, all 139 imports are libc/libm functions, no JNI, only property `ro.build.type`.
- Runtime = libmnl bytes .incbin'd into a signed Mach-O dylib (text at __TEXT+0x2000 so RW lands 16K-aligned at 0x578000; build check data-text == 0x576000) + n2mnld applies RELR + fills the 300 GOT slots with a native bionic->Darwin shim. Key ABI work: varargs trampolines (printf/fprintf/sscanf/fscanf/fcntl/ioctl; Linux va_list for vsnprintf & co, formatter reused from shim/n2shim_format.c), pthread objects by pointer, errno/flags/struct translation, epoll->kqueue, SIGEV_THREAD timers.
- Device mapping: libmnl uses the fd from cfg2 (read/write/ioctl); its ioctls are bare Linux numbers -> shim re-encodes to N2GD_IOC(n) (_IOWR 'G' n u32). DSP boot: kernel K=31 first, then a boot proxy in the shim swallows libmnl's own _BootDSP_UART_V2 frames (checks they equal the uploaded blob) and feeds the recorded FE31/FE32 acks.
- Option (b) (re-implement MNL) rejected: the DSP sends ~8 scrambled frames/s (~380 B/s, idle byte 0xCA); the navigation side is all in libmnl.
- Next phone txn (staged, gives full DSP byte stream for the host replay + proves read() after the kernel boot): gnssl11b, see GNSS_ENGINE.md 5.4. Then host: native n2mnld build + Unicorn run of the arm64 Mach-O against the replay -> NMEA; then payload-gnssd1 feeding /private/var/run/n2gnss.nmea (locbridge1).
- Expectation: indoors no fix (cold start, no EPO/time); NMEA with fix 0 / RMC V / GSV; locbridge forwards only valid fixes.

## 2026-11-12 ~21:40 HW display composition (user: "display controller composes the layers, CPU out of the UI pixel path") -- PHASE 1 ANALYSIS
Interim CPU-path fix (fbcoh, "coherent copy") was built host-only and WITHDRAWN on the user's decision (gpu/build/fbcoh-20261112-WITHDRAWN, never in a series; number 0394 reused for the HW path). Agent work dir: gpu/build/hwcomp-20261112.
**(a) Display pipeline (VERIFIED on device, phase-1 dump 2026-10-19 + current driver):** DSI0 0x1400e000 command mode (TE), DISP_MUTEX 0x14117000 (mutex 0 MOD0 0x261f7bf7: OVL0, OVL0_2L, RDMA0, COLOR/CCORR/AAL/GAMMA/DITHER, DSI0, OVL1, OVL1_2L, RDMA1 ...), DUAL PIPE: pipe0 = OVL0_2L 0x14001000 -> OVL0 0x14000000 -> RDMA0 -> ... DSI0 (left 540 columns), pipe1 = OVL1_2L 0x14101000 -> OVL1 0x14100000 -> RDMA1 (right 540). Every layer/ROI is 540x2400 (0x0960021c). The driver today only writes OVL*_2L layer 0 ADDR (+PITCH in the never-run n2scan probe) to flip between 2 panel buffers in the carve-out 0x76e10000+0x1df0000 (pitch 4352, LK CON 0x21ff). No DSC, no RSZ in use. In command mode the OVLs fetch DRAM only during a transfer (MUTEX_EN + DSI_START .. FRAME_DONE): a layer address only has to be valid from DSI_START to FRAME_DONE.
**OVL register map (READ in the MT6893 Android DRM driver, oneplus-mt6893 drivers/gpu/drm/mediatek/mtk_disp_ovl.c; per-layer stride 0x20):** INTSTA 0x08 (1 frame done, 2 underflow, 9-12 RDMAn SMI underflow), EN 0x0c (22 BYPASS_SHADOW), ROI_SIZE 0x20, DATAPATH_CON 0x24 (2 BGCLR_IN_SEL = cascade), ROI_BGCLR 0x28, SRC_CON 0x2c (bits 0-3 layer enable, 8 force relay), Ln_CON 0x30 ([7:0] plane alpha, 8 AEN, [15:12] CFMT, 23 CLRFMT_MAN premult, 24 BTSW, 25 RGB_SWAP, [29:28] source 0=mem 1=const), Ln_SRC_SIZE 0x38 (h<<16|w), Ln_OFFSET 0x3c (y<<16|x in ROI), Ln_PITCH_MSB 0x40, Ln_PITCH 0x44 ([15:0], blend selects 16-23 = 0 in Linux, 28 CONST_BLD), Ln_CLIP 0x4c, Ln_RDMA_CTRL 0xc0 (bit0), Ln_RDMA_GMC 0xc8, Ln_FIFO 0xd0, **Ln_ADDR 0xf40 (32 bit; NO address-MSB register)**. OVL_2L = 2 layers, OVL0/OVL1 = 4 layers (+3 extended): 6 physical layers per pipe, L0 bottom, OVL*_2L below OVL*. MT6885/6893: support_shadow = false (registers live; Linux writes them between frame-done and the next trigger). Formats: memory B,G,R,A (CA's 'BGRA') = CFMT 2 = CON 0x2000 (+AEN 0x100 + alpha 0xff = LK's 0x21ff); premultiplied B,G,R,A = CFMT 3 + MAN: DRM table 0x03803000 vs legacy table 0x00803000 (CONFLICT: must be tried on device). No scaler in OVL (RSZ0 0x1400c000 via the LC layer, not needed: the 1125x2436 canvas is CROPPED at (22,18), no scaling). Source crop = ADDR + sy*pitch + sx*4; dual-pipe split (mtk_drm_crtc.c 5875-5967): right pipe src_x += 540 - dx part, ADDR recomputed.
**(b) Memory addressing (VERIFIED in code/FDT):** larb0 0x14118000 / larb1 0x14119000, NON_SEC_CON(p) = +0x380+4p, bit0 MMU_EN, [15:8] address bits 32+ (IOVA bank). LK runs the display with MMU_EN=0 (physical; all LK layer ADDRs are carve-out PAs, Linux later rewrites them to IOVAs). OVL ports: OVL0 larb0 p5, OVL0_2L larb1 p6, OVL1 larb1 p5, OVL1_2L larb0 p6. With MMU off the reachable range is 0..4 GiB (32-bit ADDR; whether NON_SEC_CON bits 8-15 extend PHYSICAL addresses is NOT shown in code). XNU's RAM is 0x1_42000000..+3776 MiB = ALL ABOVE 4 GiB, and IOSurfaces are IOBufferMemoryDescriptor::inTaskWithOptions (page_size aligned, NOT contiguous). => no IOSurface is display-reachable today. Options: (1) contiguous below 4 GiB: low DRAM 0xC0000000..0xD0000000 (256 MiB) is in no FDT carve-out and no driver claim (claims: Wi-Fi 0x8fb00000+0x1500000, vcodec 0xA0000000+384M, cameras 0xD0000000..0xD8000000, JPEG 0xD8000000..0xDA800000, jpegdec 0xDA800000..0xDFC00000, GNSS rings 0xDFE00000, DVFS share 0x70000000; mblocks in live.dts) = room for ~22 full-screen 1125x2436 BGRA surfaces (11.0 MB each) and it costs no iOS RAM; physical IOSurfaces already exist and work (panel buffers: IOMemoryDescriptor::withPhysicalAddress, WC map; GPU import uses getPhysicalSegment -> works for them). (2) program the display M4U (iommu0 0x1411a000) with page tables: possible in principle (no MSB limit, scatter-gather) but M4U bring-up under XNU is untested here, shares the bank with other display/MDP masters, and a bad table = bus faults; NOT chosen for the first step. (3) hybrid = chosen: large BGRA surfaces are allocated from the display pool (1); the HW path is used when every visible layer of a swap is a pool surface, else the existing CPU path is the fallback (counted).
**(c) Refresh / atomic update (command mode):** no shadow registers: write the layer registers while no transfer runs (the present thread owns all transfers), then the existing TE-window push (state 6) and FRAME_DONE poll. Ownership: a HW-presented surface is read from DSI_START to FRAME_DONE only (panel GRAM holds the picture after that) -> its SwapWait retire moves from "copy ended" to FRAME_DONE; nothing is ever pushed again from a surface after its frame-done unless re-programmed (empty swaps on a HW frame do not re-push). Fence: flip only when nord2_gpu_surface_busy() == false for every HW layer (GPU write jobs queued/running + 0112 reservations); a HW frame is never forced while busy (bounded wait, then the swap is skipped, the panel keeps its picture). Race after the flip (app GPU writes the surface during the 9 ms scanout) is detected (busy at frame-done) and counted. The app-side guard is the IOSurface use count (traps 0/1 are no-ops in SweetSurface today) -- reverse engineering of IOSurfaceIsInUse in progress.
**Expected gain:** per present the CPU does register writes (~10 us) instead of 1.8-3.4 ms copy (50 ms worst under load) + 11 MB WC writes + 11 MB reads; the blend of 2-layer swaps also moves to the OVL. The 8.9 ms DSI transfer and the TE window stay (the fps ceiling is the panel link, ~60/90 Hz); the copy-induced late pushes (copy_gt8, tear_none_te) and the app-drawable race artifacts go away for HW frames.

## 2026-11-12 ~23:00 HW overlay R/B swap on layer 1 -> patch 0399 (gpu/build/hwcolor-20261112) -- host only, NOT on phone
- **Cause** (derived from mtk_disp_ovl.c + the photo): 0396's premultiplied CON 0x038031ff (the DRM table's ARGB8888 premultiplied, BYTE_SWAP bit 24 set) reads CA's B,G,R,A with R/B swapped on this OVL. Layer 0 (0x20ff, CFMT 2 straight) was right.
- **Fix**:
  - kern.n2fbhwpm 2 = 0x028031ff (BYTE_SWAP clear, default); pm 3 = the old value;
  - kern.n2fbhwcsw (bit0 layer 1, bit1 layer 0) flips BYTE_SWAP at run time;
  - "CON written" log plus csw/con in kern.n2fbhwstat;
  - kern.n2fbhwtest=6 colour test (R|G|B by layer 0 at rows 620-699, by layer 1 at rows 710-789; test 5 = 1,2,3,4,6);
  - kern.n2fbhwselftest=1 runs test 6 at the first mode-2/3 switch.
- **Host test** hwcolor-20261112/test/hwcolor_host_test.c ALL OK. The model now decodes CON, so it shows the 0396 bug (pm 3: 12129 px differ) and pm 2 exact.
- **Patch**: 0399-nord2-fb-hw-colour-order.patch sha256 26a0764ae574a74cd7ce6d0c5c15d251cb89f702cee4892e46f1878ef09f0e6d, on top of 0397.
  - No overlap with 0398-on0397 (both orders give an identical file).
  - The chain q10jfh + 0394..0399 applies and SweetFramebuffer.cpp compiles.
- **One-boot procedure**: DISPLAY_HW_COMPOSE.md 7.7.
- 0399 REBASED for the build chain (build_q10jfj preflight needs exact apply):
  - gpu/build/hwcolor-20261112-on0398/0399-nord2-fb-hw-colour-order.patch, sha256 0f8ca00a5b787084b5d88532ff4a9aec8b7aaf9219ab267b446e7ed19eb5a849.
  - Same change as hwcolor-20261112 (left untouched), line numbers only.
  - Chain q10jfh stage + 0394 0395 0396 0397 0398(on0397) 0399 applies with --fuzz=0 and no offsets; patched-sources-0399 == the chain result.

- Design: one table; identity 1 MiB sections for 0x76e00000-0x78c00000 (panel buffers/test slot) and 0xC0000000-0xE0000000 (pool + camera/
  JPEG/GNSS buffers) so mode A (pool, physical) shows the same with translation on or off; IOVA window 0x90000000-0xB0000000 (48 full-screen
  surfaces) for scattered pages; tables in one 580 KiB pool block (WC, < 4 GiB); TFRP -> zero page in that block. Arm (sysctl >= 1) writes
  only PT_BASE/TFRP (+INT_MAIN MMU0 bits 0-2 only if the GIC has SPI 300 masked) and refuses if any larb0/1 port already translates. Ports
  are switched ONLY in hwWriteRegs (between transfers) when a register list carries a window address (gate), off again when disarmed; lost
  MMU_EN/PT_BASE (power cycle) re-armed before an IOVA frame. Mappings keyed by surface object (no retain), unmapped in SweetSurface::free,
  evicted LRU only if no programmed OVL ADDR points inside (gate tracks all ADDR writes) and not looked up in the current planning generation.
  Every new mapping is verified by a CPU walk of every page. Cache: OVL does not snoop and IOSurfaceUnlock only marks GPU imports dirty, so
  pixels are cleaned to PoC at first map and after each write-unlock (cache maintenance, no copy).
- Sysctls: kern.n2fbiommu 0 off / 1 map-only dry run (arms + maps + walks, never hands an IOVA out) / 2 IOVA layers in single-layer frames

Miniature Foto viste a posto in modo 0 dopo ~48 scroll (celle scure stabili: da confermare).
Cosa NON e' fatto: 90 fps costanti in ogni animazione di sistema (scenario misto media 81,6; pannello 89 Hz), CPU 100% fuori in uso intenso (pool 256 MiB pieno), verifica visiva miniature in modo overlay, GPS (assente), camera/GPS non nella stessa immagine ("one big build" non fatta), IOMMU/0402c/4L mai provati, apertura/chiusura app a mano oltre lo scenario.
Rischi: 0405 alza la soglia CPU a 2200 MHz con UI attiva (batteria 43,0->43,2 C nel test, ma partiva calda); il vecchio q10jga (n2gov=0) scalda molto (+8,8 C): non usare.
Ripristino se serve: kernel q10jfk (920e3007) o q10jfh (503c38d5); undo payload: apps-20261104/payload-fbhwctl-undo.

## 2026-11-13 Wi-Fi 802.1X follow-up: 0452 + 0453, image q10jhj = q10jhe + both (host build only, NOT on the phone)
- kern.n2wifi_8021x is now a bit mask, default 0x11: 1 802.1X joins, 2 PTK rekey + EAP re-authentication on the link (0452, default OFF: as in
  q10jhe the link drops and rejoins), 0x10 handshake-complete message (0453, ON). Everything of q10jhe behaves the same with 0x11 except 0x10.
- 0452 (wifi8021x-20261113; ~2.1 KB text): e8 engine answers message 1 on an authorized link with a candidate key set kept outside struct nwp
  (SNonce = HMAC-SHA256(KCK, ANonce||SPA)); message 3 must verify under it and repeat the installed GTK, else it is dropped and nothing changes;
  then M4, PTK command, no GTK/data-path action. EAPOL-Key leaves encrypted once the PTK is in use (e8 copy of wifi_wpa_nst.c, now generated);
  the pairwise replay counters restart 100 ms after the key command (frames under the old key may still sit in the RX ring). Re-authentication:
  EAP packets pass as before, an EAP-Request on the open port makes the glue hold the AP's message 1 until eapolclient sets the new MSK.
- 0453 (~0.25 KB): verified in eapolclient: "4-way handshake complete" = IOServiceAddInterestNotification(kIOGeneralInterest) on the service two
  levels above the BSD-name registry entry, messageType 0xE0000130 (kIOMessageServicePropertyChange); "force renew" (DHCP) follows (inferred).
  The supplicant client object sends that message to its provider and two ancestors when the keys are in place (and after a rekey).
- Host: test/run-host-tests.sh HOST_TESTS_8021X_OK (test/host-tests-20261113-q10jhj.log): engine rekey vs OpenSSL authenticator (forged M1,
  unverifiable M3, repeated M1/M3, new PMK, bit clear), owner fixture AKM 1/5 with re-authentication + rekey + replay restart + hook, timeouts,
  PSK through the wrappers, repo handover/lifecycle/open suites with the switch 0 and default. (wifi-20261113/test now tests the 0436 decoder.)
- Build run_q10jhj.sh: PREFLIGHT_OK, KERNEL OK, FAILURES none, SCANPATH_OK, known 0399 stop, markers present, boot_spare 2048 (0452+0453 = 2048).
  device-mmu-q10jhj-candidate/ui-sched/nord2-ios-metal-q10jhj-ui654fb60dvfs-cap3500-ram5088-sched.img
  sha256 aaf72b618bec2bdba2b600c7a6a2223c515d56e8cb36e0634cbab7b06aa1f507.
- NOT done, with reason: TKIP (WPA1 or TKIP group): the CI wifi_station_transport.o accepts only CCMP (key command validator: cipher 4, 16 bytes;

InstalledContentLibrary (`-[MIPluginKitBundle overlaidInfoPlistWithError:]` -> EXExtensionPointCatalog) rejects every appex whose extension point is unknown.

Why the 0296 tools went blind [V-code]: 0416 replaced sweet_fb_snap() by `return NULL` (no CPU read of the panel), so every
screenshot and every verb that looks at the screen (wake/sleep/launch/mode...) failed with result 4. `panel_off` in the status was
only ever the snapshot's info word 7 (written by a successful picture), so it stayed 0 whatever the panel did. The log text
"SWEET FB: display off" is pre-0416; today's line is "NORD2 FB BLANK: DCS display off sent: panel dark" (vsync thread, DCS 0x28)
and "NORD2 FB BLANK: DCS display on sent" (0x29). Injected fingers 8/9 go through sweet_hid_touch() like the FT3518 ones
(SweetHID touch() logs "touch N down" for any finger 0..9) - why those lines were not seen in the log is not known (live log full /
reader offset are candidates); the user saw the touches and the power key act, so delivery was never broken.

0640 (snap-20261114/0640-nord2-overlay-snapshot.patch, on the q10jcq stage; files SweetFramebuffer.cpp, new sweet_fb_snapc.h,
SweetSurface.cpp, hid/SweetHID.cpp, bsd/dev/nord2_autotest.inc):
- Screenshot = the plan on the panel composed in software, on USB request only (nothing per frame; display stays CPU-free).
  presentDone copies the planned layers' device ranges + surfaces next to fHwShownPlan (under fLock; a surface not in fHwHeld is
  never named). snapHw copies plan/ranges and retains the surfaces under fLock, drops it, composes. Composition = the register plan
  slot by slot per pipe (2L L0, L1, 4L L0..3 over black), CON decoded with the 0399 colour model, AEN/plane alpha straight (pm 0)
  or premultiplied (MAN), packed 4:2:2 via sweet_fb_yuv_ref_rgb + CLIP; the 0550 band pieces are plan slots, so the rotated band
  comes out as the panel shows it. Unreadable/unmodelled slot -> MAGENTA rectangle + flag "marked-magenta" (never guessed).
  Pixels read by sweet_surface_snap_read(): only mappings the driver already has (buffer, pool, heap, purge sink, existing
  kernelMap), else IOMemoryDescriptor::readBytes under a non-blocking wod hold; cacheable ranges CIVAC'd first. No new mapping,
  no ml_io_map. Kill switch sysctl kern.n2snap=0 (refusal 20); 21 = no overlay frame shown yet; 22 = no memory (7.8 MB buffer once).
- Status (wLength >= 128, old 80-byte answer unchanged): words 20..31 = panel flags (iOS display-off request, DCS display off
  sent = dark, overlay on, band rotation live, last snapshot flags/ms), DBV sent | target, brightness request nits 16.16, presents,
  HID dispatch counters (injected touch reports, injected downs | key reports, all touch reports, touch/button clients, last
  injected x,y, injected reports with no client), magic 0x534e0001. Lock-free racy reads.

## storage-20261114: growing the iOS root volume 16 GiB -> 107 GiB, and tooling for the grown volume (2026-11-14 ~03:05, STORAGE agent)
Problem: Camera shows "iPhone Storage Full" because the HFSX root is 16 GiB while userdata is 107 GiB. Deliverables are in $B/storage-20261114 (NOT run on the phone):
- `txn_grow.sh KERNEL_IMG TAG`: rescue -> snapshot -> offline 'growprep' VM (journal replay + fsck -y + rw mount/umount, so the volume ends clean with an empty journal) -> catalog check (owned []) -> delta commit -> commit_hfs_grow plan -> commit (same rescue session) -> read-only post-grow snapshot (validates the new pipeline on the real phone, resizes the sparse mirror) -> flash KERNEL_IMG (q10jcz) -> capture.
- `snapshot_only.sh TAG [KERNEL_IMG]`: rescue -> snapshot -> flash back. Writes nothing to the phone; it does refresh the host mirror.
Tool changes (each original kept as *.pre-grow):
- fastroot.py: hash_file_chunks hashes holes of a sparse file without reading them (same digests).
- snapshot_current_root_fast.py: volume size now comes from the VH (16 GiB, or grown: a multiple of 128 MiB ending before the SWEETLOG reserve). The mirror is resized as a sparse file (grows, or shrinks back after an undo). Past 16 GiB only these chunks are verified: the alternate-VH chunk, the allocation-file chunks, and every chunk with an allocated block (bitmap after journal replay) or a journal target. Everything else is free space, listed as `unverified_chunks` in the receipt and sidecar. A 16 GiB volume takes the old path unchanged.
- commit_root_delta_fast.py: a delta chunk inside an unverified (free) 16 MiB chunk gets its preimage re-based on the current device content (it holds old Android data). Verified chunks keep the strict check. The epoch re-hash skips unverified chunks, and the sidecar keeps the list.
- stock-20261114/commit_hfs_grow.py: BUG FIXED: userdata is not a multiple of 1 MiB (224657344 sectors, so the last MiB is 992 KiB). The old code died with 'short read chunk 109695' at plan time, and its 1 MiB chunk write of the partition AVH could not have worked. The partition AVH now goes through a separate verified 4 KiB write, done last and undone first. main() is split into run() so host tests can drive it.
- read_metal_probe_log.py and display-capabilities/hfsx-read.py: adb size = partition bytes, and a grown image is accepted.
- New tests: gpu/tools/test_grown_volume.py (5 tests) and test_fastroot.py (17 tests) all pass. Full rehearsal is rehearse_pipeline.py: PASS (851 s, log rehearse_pipeline.out). It ran on copies of the 02:18 mirror with a partition-sized fake phone (garbage past 16 GiB, fake SWEETLOG) and covered: grow txn, exact undo, mirror shrink, regrow, final3-undo payload on the grown volume (fsck OK, VM on the 107 GiB disk with -m 2048), 1.2 GB fill past 16 GiB (48 free-space preimages re-based), snapshots identical afterwards, undo refused after use, SWEETLOG untouched.
- Exact undo works only until iOS first mounts the grown volume (VH chunk 0 changes at mount). The undo command is `python3 $B/stock-20261114/commit_hfs_grow.py --main $MAIN --output $X/grow-undo --undo $X/grow`.

  1415, 1222) + 15 (0xFE05) = 70746 B. Fragment 1 = 1418 B in the blob, in libmnl's write and in the n2mnld replay (which sends n2b_data
  itself); both TX paths pad to 1420 B = COUNT 0x163 (355 words), ring offset 0 at bus 0x78051000. Byte-identical by construction (replay)
  and by memcmp (libmnl, boot proxy).
- [V] Header-ack -> fragment-1 gap: ladder ~1-2 ms (ack seen on a 1 ms poll, rx_close, printf, re-arm, TX), pipe 2 ms. Same.
- [V code] Ladder TX = n2gl_tx -> n2gl_dma_start: W CON, W PGMADDR, W WPTO, then n2gl_field() for WPPT, COUNT and START: each = read,
  write, READBACK and a console printf ("write %#x mask ..."); i.e. after the START write: one readback of START + a printf, THEN the
  INTSTA/STATE poll; stop = n2gl_field(START) + n2gl_field(ACKINT), each with readback + printf, no STATE read.
  Pipe TX = n2gq_tx -> n2gl_dma_start_q: W CON, W PGMADDR, W WPTO, RMW WPPT, RMW COUNT, RMW START (no readback, no printf), then the
  INTSTA poll starts within ~1 us: 21-24 INTSTA reads (traces: hang5 24, hang6 24, hang8 21, hang9 24, hang10-12 23) WHILE the 355-word
  DMA runs (header: 2-3); stop = RMW START, RMW ACKINT, read STATE.

  DMA; the ladder starts polling only after a console printf (hundreds of us), when a ~25 us DMA has normally finished. The vendor never
  polls during a TX (waits for the DMA-done IRQ). [I] candidate mechanism: AP reads on the GPS bus colliding with the BGF DMA ->
  corrupted fragment / bridge state -> the DSP ROM acts on it ~1-3 ms later. Not proven.

## 2026-11-14 ~20:00 Safari pages black -> root cause: Metal XR formats refused in com.apple.WebKit.GPU; fix payload webxr1 (host + VM rehearsal only, NOT on the phone)
- Symptom (user photo IMG_20261114_185349): Safari toolbar/address bar draw, the page area is black, progress bar barely started.
- [V log perf1a, 19:21 capture, Safari on apple.com] the only WebKit error: `NORD2_RW E SURF <com.apple.WebKit.GPU> no drawable: pixel format 554
  is a ten-bit XR format ... (MiniIOSurface.cpp substitutes 'w30r') ... refused [repeat 4]`. No WebContent/GPU/Networking CRASH, jetsam,
  EXC, sandbox deny or JIT line. Older runs (q10dt, q10g8, night3..7, recov2/4) show the same: com.apple.WebKit.GPU creates the page
  tiles as 'w30r' IOSurfaces (1125x1905, 1125x1500, ... = the 375-pt-wide page at 3x; transparent layers 'b3a8'), then CoreAnimation's
  Metal renderer inside the GPU process asks Nord2Metal for a Metal 554 (BGR10_XR) texture over them (`drawable texture usage 0x1 ->
  0x5 (format 554 1125x1905)`, render target) -> refused; backboardd asked 554 too in older runs (50 refusals). Nothing is ever drawn
  into the tiles -> black page. Why XR: to iOS this is an iPhone X (wide-colour display), so WebKit picks 10-bit extended-range
  backing stores. JIT/sandbox/WebContent are NOT involved (inferred from the absence of any such line; WebContent stays up).
- Two refusals stacked: Nord2Metal's import (redwooddrawable.m rwd_formats: 550-555 'substituted' -> refused) and the library itself
  (air_metal.c rwa_pixel_formats had no 550-555: textures AND render pipelines with a 554 attachment refused, "no Gallium equivalent").
- The kernel (MiniIOSurface.cpp:468-479) already allocates 'w30r'/'l10r'/'w30R'/'b3a8' as plain one-plane 'BGRA' of the same geometry
  and reports 'BGRA' (SURF USE lines: fmt 0x42475241), so the memory IS 8 bits a channel.
- FIX webxr1 (dir gpu/build/webxr-20261114, src = y2s99b-shaders/merged-src + webxr1.diff): library table 550/552 -> B8G8R8A8_UNORM,
  551/553 -> B8G8R8A8_SRGB, 554 -> B8G8R8X8_UNORM, 555 -> B8G8R8X8_SRGB (no-alpha XR samples alpha 1, as Metal's BGR10_XR); Nord2Metal
  serves 550-555 over a 'BGRA' surface in place (rwd_format_of_metal / rwd_fourcc_serves, rwd_xr8_on) and adds RenderTarget usage for
  550/551 like 552-555. Writer and reader both go through the same table, so colours agree; lost: values outside [0,1] and 2 bits.
  Switch /var/db/nord2-metal/no-webxr (read once per process; NB a sandboxed process that cannot stat it treats it as absent).
  One log line per process at first XR use: `NORD2_RW I WEBXR webxr1 on: Metal formats 550-555 served as 8-bit BGRA/BGRX ...`.
- Build: src/build.sh (10 s): Nord2Metal 36f755ea01782f84..., libredwoodair.dylib 9f263e6ff8255b19... (built twice identical); control
  base-src -> fe4ecc9f / 7c0c5aba = the installed shader99b pair (exact). Host test (softpipe) host/build-webxr-test.sh +
  src/webxr_host_test.c: new lib: 550-555 created as RT, cleared, read back with the right B,G,R(,A) bytes incl. sRGB, 556 still refused
  (ALL OK); base lib: 550-555 all refused (FAIL, as expected). Not testable on host: Panfrost's BGRX render path on the Mali, the
  CoreAnimation/WebKit side.
- Payload: guest-webxr1.sh / guest-webxr1-undo.sh, payload-webxr1{,-off,-undo}, owned-webxr1.json; accepts only shader99b (fe4ecc9f +
  7c0c5aba), backups *.pre-webxr1, record 'webxr1'. Fake-root rehearsal rehearse-webxr1.sh REHEARSAL_OK (install/again/undo byte-identical,
  -off switch, foreign switch kept, fallback undo, 8 refusals, shader99b undo still works after). VM rehearsal rehearse-vm.sh on the
  current mirror (root ba2f4e2f): webxr1 / webxr1-off offline EXIT 0, catalog EXIT 0 (changed 5 / 6, outside_owned_paths []); undo on the
  mirror = no-op, catalog changed 0. (The undo guest prints INSTALL_DONE too: generic_update_offline.py requires it; NB guest-shader99b-undo.sh

- Txn: webxr-20261114/txn_webxr.sh KERNEL_IMG TAG (kernel unchanged: q10jfin), VARIANT=webxr1-off for an A/B, UNDO=1 back to shader99b.

## 2026-11-14 ~20:30 PERFORMANCE: capture perf1a analysed, log analyser n2perf.py, fixes bigpool1 (userland) + 0620/0621 (image q10jperf1) -- gpu/build/perf-20261114
Capture: autocycle/runs/perf1a (T0 19:21:13, user: home, App Library, Maps pan/zoom, Magnifier, Safari, switcher, CC/NC, free use) on q10jfin + fin1/sbshift2/api99a/final3/prod9/shader99b/gnssfix22.
Tool: `python3 gpu/build/perf-20261114/tools/n2perf.py <xnu-live.log> [--peaks N] [--csv out.csv] [--json out.json] [--from T --to T] [--all|--events-only]`
(0.3 s for a 28k-line capture). Clock = sum of 'NORD2 SYS: win_ms' (2 s rows; wall ~ T0 + t, +-10 s). Prints: per-row timeline (CPU, L/B MHz, GPU
MHz/cap, GPU busy, jobs, queue wait avg/max, job total max, presents, active fps, short gaps, drops ready/nosw, late ticks, touch Hz/gap, memory,
process launches, foreground FB client, events), phases by foreground FB client, the N worst peaks with the events around them, a summary
(on-time share, touch rate, GPU, respawn loops, battery/thermal, memory/AS/IOMMU, userland messages), and (with 0621) every stutter event
with its uptime and cause plus presents per second. Cumulative counters (GPU AS, FB IOMMU, SWAPWAIT, FB HW, FENCE) become per-row deltas.
Derived: HW-active = PRFCNT gpu cycles / (win x clock) vs driver busy (in flight); Mpix/s; bus GB/s.

Findings perf1a [V-log unless marked]:
- Phases: home/App Library 0-226 s (static 11.3/s status animation; scroll windows 60-89 fps); Maps 226-306 s: 47 fps median, 52 % of
  intervals on time, drops 'nosw' (app late) 3061 vs 'ready' 73, GPU in flight ~40 %, HW active ~35-47 %, CPU 31 % (one core 60-70 %);
  Magnifier 308-350 s: 10-14 fps, GPU in flight 87-89 %, HW active 76-79 %, mean queue wait per job 40-49 ms (max 205 ms), job run max 36.6 ms
  every window; Safari 352-432 s: 80-89 fps (good), memory avail down to 708 MiB with pageins up to 20k / 2 s at 360-376 s, one
  ReportMemoryException at ~352 s, MEMGOV 'no victim'; Photos/switcher 432-468 s 46-77 fps; battery 38.6 -> 45.5 C, thermal level 1 at
  41.4 C, 2 at 43.5 C, 3 at 45.5 C (GPU cap 836 -> 805 -> 654 -> 512, CPU caps too).
- 1 MAPS (cause, [V-log]): Nord2Metal buffer churn. Maps re-creates big GPU buffers all the time: np stats pid 13832 creates 4573 /
  closes 3707 in ~80 s; 'NORD2 GPU MAP' ~50 maps/s of 12-44 MiB (~1.1 GB/s of fresh, zeroed, page-walked memory; 0400 zero-skip is off for
  the boot: LAT2 vfail=1); userland SLOW lines: newTextureWithDescriptor 316 x avg 16 ms (5.1 s), newBufferWithLength 99 x 12.5 ms (1.2 s),
  on the render thread -> the 'app late' drops. The userland pool (nord2_pan.c) never kept anything above its largest class (16 MiB):
  'np pool: allocation of 43452 KiB refused'. [I] the 44 MiB buffers = full-screen 4x MSAA colour (1125x2436x4x4), the 12 MiB = full-screen
  depth/intermediates that Apple GPUs keep memoryless.
- 2 MAGNIFIER (cause, [V-log]): the camera preview is processed at the full 4096x3072 sensor size: 'camera ISP: 5.1 s of 4096x3072 from
  4096x3072 ... the ISP pass over 4096x3072 places: 51 renders' (~10 renders/s, 8.9 passes, wait 39 ms each) + mediaserverd
  'VTMTSComputeFunction' dispatches with 38-41 ms commits (VideoToolbox pixel transfer of that picture). One 36.6 ms compute job at a time on
  JS1 (the vertex/tiler/compute slot, nord2_gpu_hw.c n2hw_select_slots: slot_compute = slot_vertex_tiler = 1) and no preemption
  (try_start: one job per slot, oldest id first) -> backboardd's own vertex/tiler jobs wait behind it -> the WHOLE UI at 10-14 fps.
  Fix belongs to the camera pipeline [not done here]: preview from the binned 2048x1536 'cells' picture (the ISP already did 'the ISP pass
  over 2048x1536 places' for a 4096x3072 output in an earlier session) or a 1080p-class output for preview-only sessions; GPU clock acting
  (decisions-only today: 654 MHz while busy 87 %, cap 805-836) would give at most +23-28 % and more heat.

  overlap = deep scheduler change, untestable without the phone).

0630 (nord2_gpu_core.c/.h, Nord2GPU.cpp): a second chain is written to the slot's NEXT registers while one runs, when hardware order suffices:
  (same) the only older unfinished job of the context is the chain running on that slot (consecutive compute or fragment jobs; a slot runs chains in order
  with end-clean/start-clean+invalidate, kbase relies on this) or (cross) the job is the oldest of its context and the running chain is another context's.
  Never behind a stopping chain or a render (two-phase) job. Completions read the kbase_job_done way (nr_done = chains in slot - current active - NEXT
  waiting; on a failure NEXT is evicted (COMMAND_NEXT=NOP, HEAD_NEXT check) before the IRQ clear and requeued; the done-then-fail race re-reads RAWSTAT);
  stops are flag-targeted HARD_STOP_0/1 (JOBCHAIN_DISAMBIGUATION: tTRx feature in vendor r32p1 mali_base_hwconfig_features.h); a NEXT chain gets no
  deadline until it moves up; MMU kill / close take back or stop it; reset clears it. Expected gain [I]: hides the IRQ+bottom-half handoff only between
  contexts on a slot and for same-slot runs (Magnifier same~40/2 s); the Maps single-context c/f/c/f chain is unchanged (cross-slot) -> small in Maps.
  Kill: boot-arg n2jn=0 or n2gdv +4096 (n2gdv=4105) = exact pre-0630 code paths; sysctl kern.n2gjsnext=0 stops new NEXT writes.

- Expected [I]: with LVTS readable, levels 1/2 start 2 / 1.5 C later on the battery -> in a perf1a-like session roughly half of the level-2/3 time becomes
  level 0/1 (more sustained CPU and GPU clock, battery up to 46 C). Without LVTS: same as before except level 4 at 46 instead of 47 C (slower above 46 C).
- Risk: first LVTS register writes ever (thermal controller only; protection/interrupt registers never written); a bad decode is filtered by the plausibility window,
  a real hot SoC lowers clocks earlier than before. Kill: n2gdv +16.
DRAM 4266 [verdict: not done, V-code/log]: the DRAM rate is fixed at 3733 Mbps with DVFSRC disabled (basic_control en 0, sw_req 0). Moving it needs the DVFSRC
  configuration of helio-dvfsrc-mt6893.c (QoS/request tables), the SPM vcore-DVFS firmware + the DRAMC shuffle switch, and VCORE through the SPM's pwrap channel;
  0633's pwrap queue serves single MT6359P register writes on ni_thread, not this. A wrong step = DRAM hang = instant reset with no log. Peak gain +14 % bandwidth,
  measured need 10 of 30 GB/s. Not attempted.
RAM [verdict: no safe gain, V-notes/code]: physical 8 GiB = 0x40000000..0x240000000. iOS gets 0x100000000..0x23e000000 (5088 MiB) = the whole upper bank except the
  top 32 MiB; the low bank 0x40000000..0xffffffff is the vendor carve-outs and our own pools (CCCI 0x8a000000, Wi-Fi 0x8fb00000, vcodec 0xA0000000+384M, display pool
  0xC0000000-0xD0000000, cameras 0xD0000000-0xD8000000, JPEG 0xD8000000-0xDFC00000, GNSS 0xDFE00000, DVFS share 0x70000000, ...). XNU here takes one contiguous
  range (gPhysBase/gPhysSize; the 5088 window needed binary patches of wifi_rom_xnu.o / sweet_touch.o and the ram5g loader). At most +32 MiB is reachable: not worth
  a loader change. The real lever is the 2.9-3.3 GiB WIRED (GPU surfaces ~1 GiB + GPU private 0.7-1.5 GiB): GPU/userland agents' area (bigpool1 holds <= 100 MiB more
  per GPU process while idle, released on pressure); no kernel change made.

## 2026-11-14 ~23:30 gfxall3 = gfxall2 + shader file cache + per-draw state cache + upload batching + set*Bytes ring (host + fake-root + VM rehearsal only, NOT on the phone) -- gpu/build/gfx200-20261114 (all3-src, shipall)
Parts (each with its own switch file in /var/db/nord2-metal/, read once per process):
- shadercache (library; replaces Mesa's pan_disk_cache.c, built into a copy of libpanfrost.a by build.sh like gpupipe1's pan_jm.c):
  Panfrost already asks its disk-cache hooks before compiling every shader variant (pan_shader.c panfrost_shader_get) -- this build has no
  Mesa shader cache, so they were stubs. Now a file cache /var/db/nord2-metal/cache/<sha1>.pc: key = SHA-1(format/compiler tag
  N2PC_TAG, struct sizes, Panfrost's NIR SHA-1 of the uncompiled shader, the variant key) = Mesa's own keying; file = magic/version/
  key/payload length/payload SHA-1 + Mesa's payload (binary, pan_shader_info, sysvals); every field checked, anything else is a miss;
  written to a private temp file then renamed; read-only when the directory is not writable (sandbox); store cap 4096 per process.
  Expected [I]: from the second launch of a process on, the Valhall backend compile (host 0.3-6 ms per shader; most of the ~5 ms per
  pipeline seen in perf1a) is a file read; the AIR->NIR front end still runs. NOT done: asynchronous pipeline creation, launch warm-up
  (the cache serves the second launch; nothing precompiles before first use). Switch no-gfxall3-shadercache.
- statecache (library): consecutive draws keep the framebuffer bound and skip re-binding identical state objects (blend, dsa, rasterizer,
  vs, fs, vertex elements); before, every draw set the framebuffer and reset it to empty afterwards, so Panfrost dirtied and re-emitted
  ALL state at every draw (panfrost_get_batch_for_fbo -> panfrost_dirty_state_all). Every other library entry point gives the kept
  framebuffer back and forgets the cache first (rwa_g3_drop inside RWA_GUARD), so flushes, clears, blits, dispatches, destroys behave
  exactly as before. Panfrost re-selects the fragment variant on framebuffer changes by itself (pan_cmdstream.c
  panfrost_update_active_prim). Switch no-gfxall3-statecache.
- uploadbatch (Nord2Metal): buffer->texture copies used to wait for the whole GPU before EACH copy (MapKit snapshots: 120-346 per command
  buffer); now the first copy of a run in a commit waits, the next ones only if some other step ran in between (a copy only writes a
  texture, which Gallium orders itself; the wait is for the source buffer's bytes). Switch no-gfxall3-uploadbatch.
- bytesring (Nord2Metal): -setVertexBytes:/-setFragmentBytes: of <= 4 KiB copied into a 64 KiB buffer owned by the encoder at 256-aligned
  offsets instead of one new MTLBuffer per call. Switch no-gfxall3-bytesring.
  (-setBytes: of compute encoders unchanged.)
Log (with the GFX200 line, every 10 s while something moved; both need no-gfx200 absent):
  'NORD2 GPU GFXALL3: pid= name= statecache draws= fb-skipped= binds-skipped= drops= | shadercache mode=(0 off,1 ro,2 rw) hit= miss= stored=
   rejected= store-failed= compile=ms read=ms | uploads waits= skipped= | bytesring sub= chunks='

already parses the proposed F..I lines), tools/shaderstats.py (per-function Valhall stats of a metallib with the shipping translator),

shaderstats/*.tsv, afbc_model.txt.
Findings (perf1a, GPU at 654 MHz) [V = log/code/host verified, I = inferred]:
- [V-log] Active windows: GPU HW busy 35-39 % (home scroll, Maps, Safari; p90 46-66 %) = 3.9-4.4 ms per 11.2 ms refresh; Photos/switcher
  55 % (p90 64 %) = closest to GPU-bound; Magnifier 77 %. Fill needed at 90 Hz 7-23 % of the G77 MC9 peak; DRAM 3.8-5.0 GB/s of 29.9.
- [V-log] Shader cores are latency-bound: texture filter idle waiting for data 41-68 % of fragment-active cycles (90 % at idle), FMA
  density 0.02-0.09, 4.6-8.7 core-cycles per quad, mean DRAM read latency 310-370 ns. => clock scales sub-linearly [I].
- [V-log] Maps: ~42 jobs per frame, ~3.2 ms of ~11.6 ms GPU-side frame time is irq + bottom-half handoff (77 us/job).
- [V-log] Magnifier: kernel cleans ~4.1 GiB/s of CPU cache (~87 x 48 MiB/s, one per ISP pass), 174+139 us maintenance per job, ~22 %
  of a core inside the bottom half under the driver lock; lock hold up to 11.6 ms, BH wake up to 10 ms, one n2c_poll up to 5 ms.
  Maps: every new 44 MB MSAA texture cleaned once (~0.7 GiB/s); lock hold up to 8.8 ms, waits 14.9 ms.
- [V-log+code] backboardd's jobs carry > 32 buffers: every compositor job is 'full' (46/46 at idle) = whole-context maintenance and never
  'precise' -> excluded from 0632's overlap. N2C_JOB_BOS 32.
- [V-code] L2 clean+invalidate at the start of EVERY job, no FLUSH_REDUCTION; kbase r32p1 (same tTRx: FLUSH_REDUCTION, CLEAN_ONLY_SAFE,
  FLUSH_INV_SHADER_OTHER) skips start flushes for same-context follow-ups.
- [V-code] all OPPs at VGPU 750 mV; vendor table: 654 MHz @ 643.75 mV, 512 @ 600, 350 @ 550 => +36 % dynamic power at 654; shader cores
  never power-gated, GPU never powered down (vendor: cores off after 0.4-0.8 ms idle, MTCMOS+buck off when idle).
- [V-code] scheduling = global FIFO by job id, no compositor priority, compute shares JS1, one 128-record table / 96 per context.
- [V-host] Metal constant buffers other than index 0 are LD_BUFFER loads, not FAU push constants (pan_shader.c pushable_ubos = BIT(0)).
  Recompiled with every CB pushable: CoreAnimation's whole blur chain loses its loads (downsample_4 61 -> 48 inst, bound ls 6 -> t 1;
  downsample_8 regains full occupancy); modelled cycles QuartzCore x1.92, VectorKit x1.36 (Mesa's model, pessimistic for uniform loads).
- [V-host model] AFBC-like estimate on UI screenshots: 10-36 % of linear (real AFBC ~40-60 % saving [I]); bandwidth is not the limit, so
  AFBC is an energy item here.
- [V-log] battery 40.0 -> 44.9 C in the 226-468 s heavy segment (1.2 C/min); 24 % of DECISION rows at thermal level 3, 26 % at level 2.
Top 10 (rank) / order of application: (1) ship q10jfinal1 + gfxall2, then q10jfinal1f, then + gfxall3 (attributable steps);
(2) T1 telemetry patch (PRFCNT F..I lines, per-context GPU time, flush/maintenance reasons, job-size histogram; log-only);
(3) cache maintenance off the critical path (ISP buffers GPU-only/tracked, per-job list 32 -> 128 = ABI v4, work outside the global lock);
(4) compositor-first scheduling + chunked compute dispatches; (5) per-OPP vendor voltages + idle shader-core power gating (on 0633's rail
code); (6) kbase-parity L2 policy (FLUSH_REDUCTION, INV_SHADER_OTHER instead of CLEAN_INV when no CPU/foreign-dirty buffer, no end clean
for GPU-private outputs); (7) push constants for every CPU-mapped constant buffer; (8) GPU IRQ + bottom half on a big core;
(9) read-only shader cache readable by sandboxed apps (gfxall3's /var/db cache does not serve them); (10) one memory budget for all GPU
pools + pressure release (bigpool 100 + rtpool 256 + heap 32 MiB per process vs Safari's 708 MiB available).
Order: 1 -> 2 -> {3,4,8} one kernel step -> 6 alone (A/B) -> 7 (+9) -> 5 last (silicon-level). Do not combine 6 or 5 with anything new.
Not to do now: DRAM 4266/DVFSRC, soft-stop preemption, JS2 compute by default, AFBC IOSurfaces, 2 MiB pages before measuring, a custom CA
blur, always-max-clock images, maintenance shortcuts without a dirty-epoch rule, priorities without aging, raising battery limits beyond 0643.
Pass/fail table, interaction matrix (0632+gpupipe1+msaartt, rtcopy+precise maintenance, pools vs memory, q10jfinal1f's three firsts) and
the validation protocol: sections 5-6 of the document.

  the validation of the codegen: CoreAnimation's blur chain loses every LD_BUFFER (downsample_4 61 -> 48 inst, bound ls 6.0 -> t 1.0;
  downsample_8 back to 2 threads), Mesa model x1.92 QuartzCore / x1.36 VectorKit (shaderstats/quartzcore-push.tsv, vectorkit-push.tsv);
  the real gain lies between 1.0x and that. air_metal.c bind_stage now hands user_buffer = the buffer's mapping for EVERY constant-buffer
  slot (was slot 0), which is what panfrost_emit_const_buf (pan_cmdstream.c, Redwood bounds check: a word past the binding reads 0)
  copies pushed words from at the draw; the GPU address still serves loaded words. The push mode is part of the shader cache key
  (N2PC_TAG -> 'nord2-pancache-2 ... gfxall4' + a push byte), so a pushed binary never serves the other mode. Known limit [I]: a constant
  buffer the GPU wrote earlier is pushed from the CPU's view (Metal apps write constants from the CPU; CA does) -- glitches that go away
  with gfxall4-nopush = this. Switch no-gfxall4-push.
- read-only cache (library pan_disk_cache.c): lookup order = the shared /var/db/nord2-metal/cache (rw for root/mobile daemons) else the
  process's own $HOME/Library/Caches/com.nord2.pancache (a sandboxed app's container: rw, so apps hit from their SECOND launch), and on
  a miss the read-only seed /usr/lib/nord2-metal-cache (made by the payload, 0755; apps' sandbox reads /usr/lib [I, not verified]).
  The seed is built from what the phone's caches hold after a usage session: shipall/seed_pancache.sh reads the mirror (refreshed by the
  next transaction's snapshot) -- /private/var/db/nord2-metal/cache + every app container's Library/Caches/com.nord2.pancache --,
  checks every entry (magic, version, length, payload SHA-1) and makes payload-gfxall4-seeded + owned-gfxall4-seeded.json. Generating
  the seed on the PC is NOT done: the key is Panfrost's NIR SHA-1 after this library's panfrost finalisation, which the softpipe host
  harness does not reproduce (a key mismatch would only be a miss). Today's payload-gfxall4 ships an empty seed; counter mode +4 =
  seed directory present.
- budget (Nord2Metal): one budget for rtpool + texture pool + buffer pool = (free+inactive)/8 clamped 64..192 MiB, 32 MiB under 768 MiB
  free (Safari went to 708); enforced after every park and by the 2 s timer (render targets dropped first, then textures, then buffers;
  only what the GPU is done with); a DISPATCH memory-pressure source (warn/critical) empties all of them and calls the library's
  rwa_memory_pressure(BO cache | pool, 10 s) -- which also empties bigpool (np_pressure). Switch no-gfxall4-budget.
- asyncall (Nord2Metal): the completionHandler forms of render AND compute pipeline creation build on the utility queue in every
  process (were third-party apps only, compute never); content-keyed pipeline reuse stays third-party only. Switch no-gfxall4-asyncall.
  Warm-up: none beyond the caches (the file cache makes a second launch's compiles reads; nothing precompiles before first use).

Design (simpler than a lowered gPhysBase; loader, window, kernel image, ADT unchanged) [V-source]:

    (VM_PAGE_GET_PHYS_PAGE = index + vm_first_phys_ppnum), so the extra RAM is added the way XNU itself gives boot memory back
    (ml_static_mfree): vm_page_create(ppn) = a zone vm_page with an explicit ppnum, released to the free queue -> vm_resident.o untouched.
  - arm_vm_init.c: table n2ram_extra[] (compile-time stage), n2ram_validate (aligned, in DRAM, outside the window/each other, boot-arg -r8off
    = none), one ptov_table physmap slide per range (2 of 8 slots used before), physmap L1 count/end + extra, the granular-mapping bounds
    (real_avail_end / assert pa >= gPhysBase / block test) generalised to "window or extra range" (n2ram_mappable_end: identical for the
    window), max_mem/sane_size/mem_actual/max_mem_actual + extra before pmap_bootstrap (compressor, zone map, memorystatus size for it);
    arm_vm_prot_finalize: per 16 KiB page a write/read check through the physmap, then vm_page_create (failed pages stay out).
    Exported for drivers: nord2_ram_managed_end(pa), nord2_ram_extra_contains(pa,len).
  - pmap: pa_valid() (inline, pmap_data.h) = [vm_first_phys, vm_last_phys) AND (window OR an extra range): carve-outs between are NOT managed;
    vm_first/last_phys span everything (pa_index / pai->pa unchanged); pv/attr tables sized for the span (pmap_data.c, +1.9 MiB);
    pmap_has_managed_page() hole-aware (else every map of a heap/pool/codec descriptor would OSReportWithBacktrace on DEVELOPMENT).
  - Recompiled CI objects: only 3 -- arm_vm_init.o, pmap.o, pmap_data.o (pmap_misc/iommu/cs/ppl_interface compile to identical code: they

Order: c0 -> c1 -> c2, each only after the previous one ran a normal session.  Failure = EARLY boot hang/panic (arm_vm_init/pmap) or a
  hang at machine_lockdown (page check) -- before the UI.  Recovery: phone.py reset fastboot, fastboot flash q10jfinal1 (a800644a...) or
  q10jram8a.  Log after a hang: pmsg ring (pmsg-ramoops via the rescue / loader 'previous log preserved', sweetlog_tail.sh): lines
  'NORD2-XNU 14: ram8c extra ranges / bytes N SIZE' (arm_vm_init start), '15: ram8c physmap slide pa / va' (one per range),
  '16: ram8c max_mem / sane_size', '17: ram8c give range', '18: ram8c given / bad pages', '19: ram8c done'.  The last mark seen = where it
  stopped (14 without 15 = physmap; 16 present but no 17 = later boot / pmap; 17 without 18 = the page check of that range hung).
What to read on a booting image: 'NORD2 RAM8C: range 0x...: N pages to the VM, 0 failed the check' and 'NORD2 RAM8C: stage N, window
  0x100000000 + 5088 MiB, extra K ranges M MiB (... bad 0), max_mem X MiB, sane_size Y MiB, managed extent ...' (c1: max_mem 5265, c2: 5417);
  'NORD2 MEM: free=' higher than q10jfinal1 by ~11.3k (c1) / ~21k (c2) 16 KiB pages at idle; no 'IOMemoryDescriptor physical with managed
  page' reports; no GPU 'import ... e=' failures, no 'NORD2 FB IOMMU' refusals; Safari/Maps compressed pages and pageins below perf1a.
Risk analysis: (1) local-clang pmap/arm_vm_init codegen (c0 tests exactly this, nothing else changes); (2) physmap/pmap logic for ranges
  below gPhysBase (asserts are compiled in: a bad bound panics early -- marks 14-16 locate it); (3) first use of LK's boot buffers / the top
  32 MiB as cacheable kernel-managed RAM (Linux uses them as RAM, so no EMI MPU block expected; a firmware DMA there would corrupt user
  data silently -- the page check only proves CPU write/read at boot); (4) memorystatus/compressor see max_mem + extra before the pages
  arrive (vm_init .. machine_lockdown) -- conservative direction.  Jetsam/compressor scale with max_mem (percent thresholds): 5088 ->
  5417 MiB changes them by +6.5 %; our memgov still uses gPhysSize (5088) = slightly more conservative.
Next steps (not done): c3 = c2 + the 0440 SAFE regions (739 MiB) moved from the heap to XNU (heap off or shrunk) and dph/CHECK via
  0650-style pool lending -> XNU ~6.2-6.4 GiB general RAM; needs the heap/pool code to also check nord2_ram_extra_contains().

Correction [V-src/V-dt]: on MT6893 the generic scaler/rotator/colour converter is the **MDP** (mdpsys 0x1f000000: RDMA0-3, RSZ0-3,
  WROT0-3 (rotate/flip + output CSC), TDSHP/AAL/HDR/TCC/COLOR/FG, MDP mutex; no WDMA on this chip), fed in the camera by ISP P2/DIP
  through direct links; the display has only in-line DISP_RSZ0/1 (tile 1440 px, upscale/RPO). VDEC/VENC/JPEG are not scalers; the
  MediaTek "VPU"/APU is the AI processor. Android programs MDP from the closed userland libdpframework.so (op_meta lists: WRITE,
