Evidence [V-log]:
- perf2a-scn (q10jfinal2f + gfxall5): a ~2 s GPU stall (kernel 'GPU JOBS: n=3 fault=1 q_us=1999156', Maps 'GPU fence 1901.5 ms', 'FB HW: H6 fence
  still pending'), then 'GPU AS ... mmu_faults=2 orphan=1' ('MMU fault on an AS no context holds' = the second report of the same stalled access
  after the first one killed the context) and 1448 x '|backboardd| MESA: error: panfrost_batch_submit failed: 5' until the end: backboardd's
  GPU context was FAULTED by the kernel (every later submit EIO) -> nothing composited -> SpringBoard main thread HANG, CPU/GPU idle.
  LAT3 just before: precise=3156 overlap=1244 held=135884 (0632 pass overlap active).
- e-logs (q10jfinal1f + gfxall2-off, i.e. gfx200 off but gpupipe1 on): 'GPU JOBS: n=166 fault=1 ... stops=1', LAT3 precise=180 overlap=54; then
  backboardd's waits time out (np call 41 errno=60) and its allocations sit in new_bo_ex's wait_seq / 100 x 100 ms not-ready loop (np time
  create max 10114225 us, newTextureWithDescriptor 20239 ms, then the 'would not allocate' refusal): a CONSEQUENCE of the faulted context,
  not a budget problem (kernel budgets 768 MiB/client, no budgetReject line). shader99b (one heap, v2 submits, no overlap) never does it.
Root cause [V-code + V-host]: gpupipe1's pan_jm.c remembered which of the two rotating tiler heaps a batch's tiler context points to in a
  64-entry ring keyed by the descriptor's GPU address alone and searched it oldest-index-first ("last match wins"). Batch pools hand out the
  SAME descriptor address every time a batch slot is reused, and the heaps alternate A/B, so after the ring wrapped the lookup returned a
  stale entry: the chain went out PRECISE with the WRONG heap in its list, the kernel's 0632 overlap saw no conflict and ran pass k+1's tiler
  over the heap pass k's fragment job was still reading -> corrupted polygon lists -> a fragment job that hangs / faults -> context killed.
  Host model (gpupipe_heap_host_test.c, the functions EXTRACTED from pan_jm.c, backboardd-like sequence: 282090 passes, slots reused, same
  descriptor address per slot, A/B rotation, up to 40 open batches): gfxall5 ring returned a wrong heap 43617 times (15 %), gfxall6 0.
Fix gfxall6 (all6-src = all5-src + pan_jm.c): the heap of each live batch is kept EXACTLY per (pipe_context, batch slot) with the descriptor
  address checked; if it is ever not known exactly the chain is submitted WITHOUT an access set (not precise: never overlapped) and every
  extra heap is listed too. Nothing removed: rotation, v3/v4, overlap and all gfx200/gfxall3/gfxall4 parts unchanged.

## 2026-11-15 ~02:30 App Library backdrop BLACK with gfxall6 -> gfxall7 (pass-overlap access sets), host + fake-root rehearsal (VM below); NOT on the phone
Phone facts (orchestrator): gfxall6 fixed the Maps freeze; the App Library blurred backdrop renders black on q10jfinal2f and q10jfinal1f with
  gfxall6, was correct with gfxall5-nov4 (q10jfinal1f), black in perf2a (gfxall5, v4). Folders and fresh switcher cards fine.
Analysis [V-code, I where marked]:
- The difference between correct and black is ABI v4: with v3 (32 handles) backboardd's lists are longer than 32 -> TRUNCATED -> never
  precise -> never overlapped, whole-context CPU maintenance; with v4 (128) the compositor's chains become PRECISE for the first time.
- pan_jm.c (gpupipe1) gave each chain an access set from the batch's per-stage flags: the vertex/tiler chain counted a buffer only if its
  flags had the VERTEX_TILER stage. A texture that pass k+1 SAMPLES in its fragment stage (every downsample / blur step of the backdrop:
  it reads what pass k's fragment job just wrote) was therefore NOT in pass k+1's vertex/tiler set, and the kernel (0632 may_overtake /
  jobs_conflict, by buffer identity) let pass k+1's vertex/tiler chain start beside pass k's still-running fragment job -- contrary to
  0632's own design note ("blur chains stay serial"). Also a precise chain is CPU-cleaned only for the buffers it touches. [I] Exactly
  which hazard turns the backdrop black on the Mali (cache maintenance of the sampled/written buffers, or ordering) was not provable on
  the host; the rule violation itself is certain and shows only for the compositor once v4 makes it precise.
- rtcopy/msaartt/rtpool/pools: not involved (gfxall5-nov4 had all of them and was correct); rtpool/texpool reuse is quarantined
  (textures freed only after their command buffers completed; pools check the done sequence); completion tracking is "all <= seq".
Fix gfxall7 (all7-src = all6-src + pan_jm.c rw_pipe_acc): the vertex/tiler chain -- the only chain the kernel lets overtake -- declares
  EVERY buffer of its batch (both stages) with its write bit; the fragment chain keeps its own stage's set. A pass that reads or writes
  anything an older unfinished fragment job writes never overtakes it, and its CPU maintenance covers the whole batch; independent passes
  (Maps' separate targets) still overlap. Kept: v4, overlap, rotation, every gfx200/3/4 part.
Tests: gpupipe-acc-host-test.sh (rw_pipe_acc extracted from pan_jm.c + the kernel's conflict rule as a model, 200,000 random pass pairs:
  every dependent pair serialised, 19,858 independent pairs still overlap; the gfxall6 rule fails the same test at once: 'vt chain must
  touch a fragment-read texture'); gpupipe-heap-host-test.sh still ok. Build: library ec36ec3eccffd88c47daf8f0c6969b92fc1a4e2a2bb1b73f04860a71f3e9793d
  (twice identical), Nord2Metal unchanged 2cb9a64b56d7. Fake-root rehearsal REHEARSAL_OK incl. the current mirror (gfxall6 record):
  gfxall7 over it + undo byte-identical; gfxall1..7 from every state.

  n2hw_js_evict_next took a chain back from NEXT but kept its JOB_CHAIN_FLAG toggle, so the next chain written got the SAME flag as the current
  one; a flag-targeted HARD_STOP of the current chain that had just completed (IRQ not yet handled) then hit the next, innocent chain (trace:
  cur 5778 f1, NEXT 5780 f0 taken back (0662), 5788 written with f1, 5778 completes, core stops 5778 -> 5788 stopped while RUNNING).  Fix in
  0668: the helper flips the slot toggle back on a successful take-back.  Model: eviction gives the flag back + new invariant "NEXT never carries
  the current chain's flag"; hw_rb10_test.c checks the register-level give-back (fails on the p6 core, passes on p10).

  never under a chain, 7034 power-down/up pairs) 200k steps OK, -Werror clean, pre-0630 suite identical numbers, HW_RB_REGISTER_TEST_OK.

- Warm-L2 recovery (proposal, not built): G77 (JM) has no L2 range flush (FLUSH_PA_RANGE is a newer-GPU feature [I]), so "invalidate only the WC
  ranges" is not available; AS FLUSH_MEM flushes the whole L2 as well.  Correct options: (1) per-submit userland hint "CPU wrote buffers M since
  the last submit" (v4 mask) -> per-BO cpu_gen; START invalidates only if a touched BO has cpu_gen > last full-invalidate gen; no hint (v2/v3 or
  unknown) = always invalidate (0667 behaviour).  (2) descriptor pools cached + cleaned in prep (0661 two-phase clean is already off the lock), so
  0664's clean_seq sees them; costs CPU cleans.  Either way the gain is bounded: every chain after a fresh CPU write batch must invalidate; only
  later chains of the same batch (fragment phase after vertex, extra passes) keep the L2.  Measure first: GPUPROF MAINT l2_inv vs jobs on final2f.

## 2026-11-15 ~05:50 MDP 0677 WROT rotation offsets (q10jmdp6: copy256 PASS on hardware, rot90 all wrong), image q10jmdp7 (host only)
Phone q10jmdp6 [V-phone]: S1 copy256 exact (hw 1308 us) = first MDP DMA job ever on this port; rot90 completes (1301 us) but every pixel
wrong, VIDO_OFST_ADDR was 0.  [V-dis DpEngine_WROT::onConfigTile]: OFST is the address of the FIRST pixel written; for walks that go
right-to-left it is the LAST byte of that pixel: rot0 F0 y0*P+x0*B | F1 y0*P+(W-x0)*B-1; rot90 F0 x0*P+(H-y0)*B-1 | F1 x0*P+y0*B;
rot180 F0 (H-1-y0)*P+(W-x0)*B-1 | F1 (H-1-y0)*P+x0*B; rot270 F0 (W-1-x0)*P+y0*B | F1 (W-1-x0)*P+(H-y0)*B-1 (W x H unrotated output,
F = mirror).  With OFST 0 the rot90 walk started at the buffer start and went BACKWARDS = below the destination (into an unused
pool area; nothing else lives at pool 0x200000-0x2fffff).  Rotation direction: vendor 90 = clockwise = our reference.  The vendor
mirror is a mirror of the destination after rotation (ours: source before) -> identical for rot 0, so mirror+rotation is refused
(N2MDP_E_DST) until verified; S1/S2 tests and the service never combine them.
0677 (piece-0677/0677-nord2-mdp-wrot-rotation-offsets.patch, job.h + inc): vendor offsets; guard band BELOW the destination
(1 MiB, checked after every job -> code 5 "bytes written BELOW the destination"); on a mismatch: written-byte count, first/last
written offset and the first pixels.  Host: t_mdp_full_0677.c (WROT model now walks from OFST like the hardware) ALL OK incl. rot90/
180/270, tiled rot90, scale+rot, IOVA rot90 service blit; old offset = caught (writes below dst); run_t_mdp_pwron.py 12/12.

    ~/.local/share/ulog-src/examples/target/release/unifiedlog_iterator (log-archive mode; the full decode is 24 GB of jsonl: grep wifid
    and delete it at once, disk!). wifid lines of all boots -> autojoin-20261115/wifid.tsv (boot uuid, time, pid, message).
  - [V] wifid's CoreWiFi auto-join DOES run on every boot and after every unlock/screen event (triggers power_on, iff_up, user_wake,
    app_state, retry, aj_enabled, ...); known networks listed with autojoin=yes; the scan finds both FRITZ!Box networks
    ("Found matching network ... rssi=-67" 2.4 GHz, "-64" 5 GHz), then EVERY candidate is dropped:
    "Join candidate 'wifi.network.ssid.<redacted-ssid>' is not allowed (error=(1 'Below minimum RSSI threshold'))".
    3476 such lines over all boots in the log, the ONLY rejection reason; RSSI of the rejected candidates -58..-81 dBm. Boot 472262F6
    (08:3x, last before the mirror): 9 auto-join sessions, 50 matches, 50 RSSI rejections. No association is ever requested (no
    JOINREQ/JOINCONTROL in the kernel logs without a tap) -> 'Not Connected' until the user taps (user join skips this filter).
  - [V wifid disassembly, research/nord2/wifi/ios-abi/wifid 20H392] the error is built at 0x100128d00 (cfstring 0x100230520, code 1)
    when [candidate RSSI] < threshold; threshold = func 0x10010b0a0 = device manager +0x80 (special cases -70/-65 for networks with
    history), set at 0x1000dc8f8 from WiFiDevice +0x100. WiFiDevice +0x100 = RSSI_THRESHOLD: WiFiDeviceCreate defaults (+0xf0/+0xf8/+0x100)
    = RSSI_MIN -19, RSSI_MAX 65, RSSI_THRESHOLD 7; WiFiDeviceOpen (0x10004b8d0) does Apple80211CopyValue(0x6a = 106) and only on success
    reads RSSI_MIN/RSSI_MAX/RSSI_THRESHOLD and logs "Device RSSI bounds (%ld, %ld) with treshold (%ld)". That line is absent from every
    boot ("WiFiDeviceOpen: entering / Device power state = ON / exiting" present) = our shim's "request=106 bytes=16 status=0xe00002c7".
    So threshold 7 dBm: no real network can pass.
  - [V IO80211 dyld cache, _Apple80211GetWithIOCTL+9352] GET 106 struct = 16 bytes {u32 version=1, s32 RSSI_MIN, s32 RSSI_MAX,
    s32 RSSI_THRESHOLD} (kCFNumberSInt32Type each), name APPLE80211_IOC_RSSI_BOUNDS.

## 2026-11-15 ~12:00 MDP instead of GPU for display work: data-driven feasibility + staged plan (analysis only; logs from scratchpad, no phone)
(1) Where the GPU time goes [V-log unless marked]
- Per process (GPUPROF CTX run_us summed over the whole session log):
  Maps (perf6f-maps-ok): backboardd 76 %, Maps app 23 % (3D/vector = class e), rest < 1 %.
  Magnifier (final10-magnifier-m2 / magnifier-final2f-gfxall7): backboardd 59 / 54 %, mediaserverd (camera: our GPU ISP + VideoToolbox
  converter/rotator + preview scaler) 40 / 46 %.   Subway Surfers (subway-final5a): game 84 % (class e), backboardd 16 %.
- backboardd = CoreAnimation, by draw class (CA program names in the gfxall 5 s 'perf:' summaries; class from the name: B<mode> = blended,
  no T = untextured, Tds = downsample, Timg without B = plain textured copy, other T = filter/lookup/colour matrix):
  | session (draws)            | (c) blended composite | untextured fill/mask (no blend) | (b) textured copy, no blend | (b) downscale pass | (d) filter/other |
  | Safari+home mix (699k)     | 49.7 %                | 37.6 %                          | 8.0 %                       | 1.2 %              | 3.5 %            |
  | Safari (56k)               | 41.1 %                | 46.3 %                          | 5.5 %                       | 0.9 %              | 6.3 %            |
  | home/lock nofb (19k)       | 62.7 %                | 26.7 %                          | 3.0 %                       | 0                  | 7.7 %            |
  | home/AL diag9 (15k)        | 56.4 %                | 30.8 %                          | 4.4 %                       | 0.1 %              | 8.4 %            |
  Draw counts, not GPU time: per-pass GPU time is not instrumented [gap].  Blit encoders: ~8 log lines in a whole session (CA does not
  blit); IOSurface copies in backboardd: 0 (zero-copy already); class (a) is therefore ~0.  The no-blend textured draws are nearly all the
  first layer of a multi-draw composite pass (not separable); the only stand-alone (b) passes are the blur-chain heads (Tds4/Tds8,
  1125x2436 -> 1/4, 1/8: <= 1.2 % of draws, small targets) which feed blur/colour-matrix/composite passes in the same frame.
- Counters (GPU_PERF_ANALYSIS, perf1a 654 MHz): HW busy 35-39 % home/Maps/Safari, 55 % switcher, 77 % Magnifier; cost per quad
  latency-bound (texture starve 41-68 %), DRAM 4-5 GB/s of 30.
(2) What the MDP can take [V-code/log for MDP facts, I for estimates]
- MDP has RDMA/RSZ/rotate/CSC/copy, no blend/blur/shader -> only (a)/(b) whole-surface ops.  UI: blit encoder = none used; single-quad
  no-blend passes = blur heads only; switcher snapshots/screenshots = rare one-offs; wallpaper = PosterBoard renders, not scales.
  Camera/video: VideoToolbox VTPixelTransfer (converter/rotator/zoomer, preview scaler), CMCapture scalers, encoder input conversion,
  thumbnails (ImageIO/CMPhoto) all go through IOSurfaceAccelerator = our AppleM2ScalerCSCDriver.
- Today (final10 Magnifier): M2 calls 2659: 1329 ok = 420f -> 420f rot90 (1504x1128) at ~12.3 ms each; 1329 refused (dstfmt).
  Pixel rate ~1 px/clk/pipe at 594 MHz [I] -> 1.7 Mpx ~2.9 ms on one pipe: ~9 ms per call is overhead (per-call M4U map of ~1700 pages,
  CPU cache clean/invalidate of 2 x 2.5 MB, CPU-polled completion, synchronous return) [I].
- Hazards for UI offload: every MDP op in a CA frame = GPU job end -> kernel -> MDP (+ cache maintenance) -> MDP poll/IRQ -> GPU job start:
  >= 0.3-1 ms extra latency per hop vs 50-300 us GPU jobs; MDP writes vs GPU reads of the same surface need a fence in the GPU job graph
  (MDP is CPU-polled today); shared DRAM (negligible: 4-5 GB/s used); MDP clock MMDVFS 273-594 MHz adds power if kept up.
(3) Expected gain [I]
- UI (home/AL, Safari, switcher, Control Center): offloadable <= ~1-2 % of CA draws (blur heads) and likely < 5 % of GPU time; GPU is busy
  only 35-55 %; jank comes from CA/app lateness, per-quad latency and memory stalls -> no visible fluidity gain; in-frame GPU<->MDP hops
  would ADD latency.  Maps / games: ~0 (3D / vector).  Honest verdict: "MDP for all display operations" is NOT a UI fluidity lever here.
- Camera/Magnifier/video: real.  Converter/rotator + preview scaler ~ half of the camera GPU load (~13 of ~23 ms per frame after
  camprev1) = ~20-25 % of all GPU time in Magnifier (77 % busy -> ~55 %); plus the 20 ms/frame CPU SecondaryScaler if CMCapture takes M2;
  less heat -> fewer thermal down-steps in long camera sessions.
- Real UI wins remain: push constants/FAU (x1.3-1.9 on CA blur shaders), AFBC for private targets, L2/flush policy and job overheads,
  CA commit lateness (CPU), clocks/thermal (GPU_PERF_ANALYSIS items 3/6/7/8).
(4) Plan
- Stage 1 (days, low risk, all in the M2 service): accept the refused dstfmt requests (BGRA / other 420 variants), crop/rect and scaling;
  IOVA cache per IOSurface (map once, unmap on surface free), skip cache ops for uncached/GPU-only surfaces, IRQ completion + async
  (fence = IOSurface use count), split frames > 1 Mpx over 2 pipes -> target 1504x1128 rot90 ~3-4 ms; advertise caps so CMCapture's
  SecondaryScaler and VT preview scaler use M2.  Measure: mediaserverd GPUPROF CTX share, Magnifier GPU busy, M2 hist.
- Stage 2 (1-2 weeks, medium-high risk; only if Stage 1 data shows UI benefit): in-kernel MDP job API with GPU-graph fences (MDP job as a
  node in n2c's dependency/maintenance graph), driver offload of blit-encoder copies/scales and detected single-quad no-blend passes.
  Expected UI gain < 5 % GPU time -> recommend NOT now.
- Stage 3: video playback/encode conversions and thumbnails through M2 (falls out of Stage 1 caps); display-side layer composition (OVL
  layers in the HW FB path) is the only display-engine lever that touches UI composition, separate from MDP.

# RAPPORTO GIORNATA 2026-11-15 (mattina/pomeriggio, utente presente) — risultati misurati sul telefono
**Configurazione sul telefono ora: kernel q10jfinal13 (sha 2d7a82b5...) + userland gfxall16-seeded.** Comando userland: `cd gpu/build && VARIANT=gfxall16-seeded READS=600 gfx200-20261114/shipall/txn_gfxall.sh <img q10jfinal13> TAG`. Flash leggeri (solo kernel): `autocycle/flash_boot.sh <img>` con il telefono gia' in fastboot (aspettare `lsusb | grep 0e8d:201c` dopo `phone.py reset fastboot`; non serve il lock pesante). Rescue log dopo un crash: `ENTER=1 FB_WAIT=120 bash gnss-20261114/sweetlog_tail.sh /tmp/OUT 300` (non avviare altro kernel prima).
## Risolto
- **Safari**: causa 1 = i tile WebKit sono superfici 'w30r' (deep colour) rifiutate dal controllo gfx100a (gfxall13 le serve in 8 bit); causa 2 = CoreAnimation scarta i livelli 'b3a8' (trasparenti) perche' la domanda Apple3 di QuartzCore riceveva NO (gfxall15: YES solo per quella) + piano colore b3a8 con controllo di dimensione corretto (gfxall16). Verificato: apple.com (barra, sezioni in basso), Wikipedia (portale + it.wikipedia con testo/foto), Google con finestra di consenso, tocchi/navigazione/tastiera.
- **Wi-Fi auto-join**: wifid chiede GET 106 (RSSI_BOUNDS) all'avvio, il nostro livello rispondeva 'unsupported' -> soglia di default +7 dBm -> tutte le reti scartate ('Below minimum RSSI threshold'). Fix 0790 (soglia -80 dBm, sysctl kern.n2wifi_rssithr, 0 = vecchio comportamento). Verificato: si collega da solo ~32-37 s dopo il boot.
- **App Library blur**: gfxall10/11 (rifiuto dello snapshot MTMaterialLayer).
- **RAM**: pool grafico 1577 MiB (0650+0651+0653, regioni verificate sul device tree), 14 canary senza errori, 6665 MiB utilizzabili. RAM normale extra (fase 2) ABBANDONATA: c1/c1t/c1u (sopra la finestra) e c1w (sotto) non si avviano/si bloccano, c1v (controllo) si avvia.
- **MDP in hardware**: S1/S2/S3 passano (copia, rotazioni, flip, NV12->BGRA, NV12->NV12 con rotazione, scala NV12 anche su piu' tile, scala RGB per contenuto liscio, M4U1 IOVA sopra 4 GiB). Il servizio iOS AppleM2ScalerCSCDriver e' attivo e gestisce il 100 % delle richieste della fotocamera (Magnifier: 2990/2990, 1332/1333; 0 errori; anteprima corretta). Tempi per fotogramma 1504x1128 NV12 rot90: hw 6-9 ms, map 0.03, cache 0.32, totale ~13.9 ms; clock MDP gia' 594 MHz (TVDPLL, step 0). Ultimo giro di ottimizzazione in corso (0689/q10jmdp19).
## Analisi (non implementato)
- MDP al posto della GPU per le operazioni del display: guadagno atteso <5 % del tempo GPU per l'UI (composizione con blending 40-60 %, riempimenti 27-46 %: non fattibili su MDP; GPU occupata 35-55 %); per camera/Magnifier/video e' reale (circa meta' del carico GPU della camera, ~13 di 23 ms/frame, GPU 77 % -> ~55 %).
- Push constants: implementate (gfxall4+, switch no-gfxall4-push) ma mai misurate A/B sul telefono; L2 policy 0664: provata e tolta; AFBC su IOSurface: non fatto.
## Immagini principali
q10jfinal10 (final9 + MDP 0670-0685 + Wi-Fi 0790), final11 (+0686 NV12 dst), final12 (+0687 cache IOVA), final13 (+0688 cache superfici + log clock); standalone q10jaj1 (solo fix Wi-Fi), q10jmdp14..19. Userland: gfxall13 (w30r), 14 (limite compilazioni MSL WebKit), 15 (b3a8 Apple3), 16 (piano colore b3a8; versione finale).
## Aperto
S3->uso reale gia' attivo; ottimizzazione tempo MDP (rotazione/2 pipe); push constants A/B; Safari: video (aree nere) non verificati; Foto/Meteo/Subway invariati rispetto al rapporto precedente.

## 2026-11-15 App Store feasibility (host-only research, phone NOT touched) -- gpu/build/appstore-20261115
Question: can Apple's own App Store client + installer stack download, install and launch an app for the user's legitimate Apple ID on
this port (no SEP, no Apple hardware keys)? [V] = verified on host (mirror 11:00, its unified log, 20H392 IPSW kernelcache, dyld cache,
our XNU tree final3-20261114/chain/s + ci-39158169212 buildtree); [I] = inferred.
Evidence files: appstore-20261115/unifiedlog-store-evidence.tsv (deduplicated key lines, all boots, with counts),
appstore-20261115/FairPlayIOKit-20H392-cstrings.txt. Method: unifiedlog_iterator on autojoin-20261115/arc streamed through grep (no
24 GB decode on disk; extracts deleted).
- Flow ('Get'): AppStore.app (AppStoreKit/JetEngine) -> AMS (AppleMediaServices: bag from bag.itunes.apple.com, AMSURLRequestEncoder adds
  User-Agent incl. FairPlay device type, X-Apple-AMD / Anisette (ADI via adid + akd), X-Apple-ActionSignature = AMSMescal (FairPlay SAP via
  fairplayd), kbsync (FairPlay)) -> Apple ID auth: akd/AuthKit GrandSlam (gsa.apple.com) needs Anisette machine provisioning (ADI) ->
  amsaccountsd / accountsd store account (storefront, DSID) -> appstored (ASD) buyProduct to p*-buy.itunes.apple.com -> download
  (appstored/nsurlsessiond) -> installcoordinationd + installd (MobileInstallation, streaming unzip, containermanagerd containers,
  LaunchServices registration) -> sinf/SC_Info: account FairPlay keys held by fairplayd -> launch: exec of the cryptid=1 main binary ->
  XNU set_code_unprotect() -> text_crypter_create hook (provided by kext FairPlayIOKit) -> apple_protect pager decrypts pages with keys
  from fairplayd (HostSpecialPort 17 = HOST_UNFREED_PORT, 'com.apple.unfreed', served by fairplayd.H2).
- [V rootfs] present: AppStore.app, appstored, itunesstored, storekitd, amsaccountsd, amsengagementd, akd, accountsd, adid, lskdd,
  fairplayd.H2 (/usr/sbin, KeepAlive, MachServices com.apple.fairplayd(.versioned), com.apple.unfreed HostSpecialPort 17),
  fairplaydeviceidentityd (BAA prefetch activity), mobileactivationd, installd, installcoordinationd, mobile_installation_proxy, nsurlsessiond.

  entitlement com.apple.private.FairPlayIOKitUserClient.access, OSBundleLibraries = kpi.* only, no SEP kext dependency). Its strings:
  generateSeed / generateInFieldSeed / getEncryptedSeedSegment call **IOAESAccelerator::performAES with the GID key and the UID key**
  (AppleS8000AES hardware keys), IODeviceTree:/product product-id, PIKDecryptWithFixedSharedKey, NVRAM. So FairPlay on A11 is not SEP
  based but IS rooted in Apple's fused AES keys (GID per SoC family, UID per device).
- [V our XNU] CONFIG_CODE_DECRYPTION is on (MASTER.arm64.sweet), mach_loader set_code_unprotect(): cryptid 1 'com.apple.unfree' and
  text_crypter_create == NULL -> LOAD_FAILURE -> exec refused ("set_code_unprotect() error"). Nothing in our tree calls
  text_crypter_create_hook_set; no FairPlayIOKit, no IOAESAccelerator class in final3 sources. => no App Store (encrypted) binary can
  launch on our kernel today. (Subway Surfers/Terraria run because they are already-decrypted IPAs, cryptid 0, put in by apps_update_offline.)
- [V entitlements] fairplayd.H2 has com.apple.private.FairPlayIOKitUserClient.access + iokit-user-client-class
  com_apple_driver_FairPlayIOKitUserClient, adi-client, lskd-client. [V log] launchd: 'service inactive: com.apple.fairplayd.H2' 3699x,
  kernel 'exec fairplayd.H2' 3694x over 139 boots; its only log lines are one container lookup per run (clean exit, not a crash).
  [I strong] it exits because the FairPlayIOKit service it needs does not exist; mach clients queue on its launchd-held ports forever.
- [V log] what happens today: AppStore.app launched (1 boot, E8068FB4, 3 launches): LoadingViewController -> FlowTabBarController, every
  launch 'Loading bag from the network' + 'Encoding request for URL: https://bag.itunes.apple.com/bag.xml' and then NOTHING (no
  finish/error ever). appstored 'Timed out while waiting for snapshot bag to load' (ASDErrorDomain 515) 267x, 'Starting FairPlay service'
  each start; no AMS bag ever loaded by any process while identityservicesd's IDS bag loads ('Server bag signature verification
  succeeded') and Safari works -> network/TLS are fine. [I] the encoder blocks in a FairPlay RPC (AMSFairPlayGetDeviceType -> obfuscated
  _CjHbHx; same pattern as locationd's CLMescalSigner SAPInit hang) -> even BROWSING the store is blocked by fairplayd.
- [V log] Apple ID sign-in (Settings, Preferences FetchAnisette 751 s): akd 'ADIProvisioningStart succeeded' (gsa midStartProvisioning
  HTTP 200) then 'ADIProvisioningEnd failed. Error: -42410' -> 'No Anisette for you today' (AKAnisetteError -8004/-8005/-8007), every
  boot. akd 'Attestation error com.apple.devicecheck.error.baa -10001 <- MobileActivation -1 <- OSStatus -25293' (BAA device identity
  key/cert absent: hactivation, synthetic ECID 0x5357454554000001, no serial/syscfg in our ADT). adid: 'Failed to copy the SysCfgDict MG
  key', 'Could not get bluetooth address', 'A4: -45052'. Local iTunes account 'username = local, storefront = (null)', no DSID.
- Other checks: AMFI emulation (sweet_amfi.c vnode_check_signature) sets CS_SIGNED for every signature, no chain/profile check -> an
  Apple-signed app would pass signature policy (only page hashes are checked by XNU). AKS 'no passcode, unlocked' fine for data
  protection. 'accountsd privilege 1002' = PRIV_GLOBAL_PROC_INFO (benign). App containers via containermanagerd work (sideloaded apps run).
- Blockers ranked: (1) FairPlay: fairplayd needs FairPlayIOKit, whose device binding uses the GID/UID hardware AES keys -> cannot be
  provided legitimately on MT6893 (emulating it would mean reproducing Apple's GID-key secrets = DRM circumvention; NOT pursued). Without
  it: no bag/User-Agent, no Mescal, no kbsync, no account FairPlay authorization, no sinf, no decryption at exec. HARD WALL.
  (2) Anisette/Apple ID: ADI provisioning fails on device identity (no serial/syscfg/BT; possibly also the fairplayd/lskd dependency);
  inventing a serial or borrowing a real iPhone's identity = impersonation, not acceptable. (3) BAA / DeviceIdentity / activation record /
  APNs certs: Apple-minted for a real ECID+SEP key; absent by construction (hactivation). Probably not strictly needed for a password
  purchase, but cannot be provided. (4) kernel text_crypter provider: trivial to hook, but only meaningful with genuine keys from (1).
- Verdict: NO-GO for the genuine App Store download+install+launch on this port. Legitimate fallback that already works: install apps the
  user builds/signs themselves or open-source/unencrypted IPAs (cryptid 0) with the existing offline installer; optional small
  host-only improvement: make fairplayd absence fail fast (stop KeepAlive respawn / give clients an error) so AppStore/locationd-style
  hangs become clean errors -- cosmetic, does not enable purchases.

  IOServiceGetMatchingServices for FairPlayIOKit before it exits; screenshot of App Store spinner. Not needed for the decision.

## 2026-11-15 ~18:30 gfxall17: Terraria (landscape-only) on the GPU -- rotated display-surface textures served (host + fake-root rehearsal; NOT on the phone)
- Root cause [V-log, autocycle/runs/gnssd3j/ui-usb/xnu-live.log, also y2s33 on 4 Nov]: when Terraria comes to the front (HID GraphicsOrientation=4),
  backboardd's compositor (CA::OGL::MetalContext::get_surface) asks for the 1125x2436 display surfaces (2, 3, 51) as 2436x1125 textures with the
  private MTLTextureDescriptor rotation (3 = 270, "rotated scan-out"; Oct-26 QuartzCore read: only 0 or 3 at that site) -> our driver refused
  every one ("no drawable: surface 3 is 1125x2436 and the descriptor asks for 2436x1125", x64+; also "surface 67 is 1125x699 ... 699x1125").
  CA does not test the nil -> the compositor draws nothing while Terraria is in front (frozen frame, only the switcher shows it). Terraria
  itself renders fine (its own 2436x1125 drawable, y2s33 usage fix). Apple GPUs address rotated textures in hardware; the Mali cannot.
- Fix (all17-src; Nord2Metal 30bb1c62cbc84ebe6add4f651809cbb804bd004f9f4fdc2d672d3b21f22d5fad, library
  fd4cdc14ae6b9e58a2808807257937a4f240e95d8e8445892b272af4b51817f8, b1 == b2):
  library: rwa_texture_rotate(dst, src, mapping 1/2/3) = one full-screen nearest-sampled GPU pass (reuses the ycbcr quad/fixed state).
  driver: a descriptor with rotation 1/2/3 -> surface imported unrotated (WxH) + own landscape texture (logical, what CA draws in); turned in
  once at creation; every command buffer that renders into it gets one rotate pass into the surface queued before its fence; read-only rotated
  textures turned in again when the seed moves or after 8 ms. -[texture rotation] now reports the asked rotation.
  Direction [I, unverified]: rotation 3 = memory(x,y) = logical(y, W-1-x) (stored picture = logical turned 90 deg clockwise). If upside down:
  switch file gfxall17-rot-flip (variant gfxall17-flip-seeded). Kill switch: no-gfxall17-rot (variant gfxall17-norot = old refusal + surf-all).
  Nothing changes for processes that never ask for a rotated texture (rw_rot_on only runs when rotation != 0).

## MDP 0691: recovery + scale policy after the q10jfinal19 mediaanalysisd failure; image q10jfinal20 (host only, NOT on the phone)
- Phone log (scratchpad l5b-9.log ~3320-3470) [V]: request 0x2b7 -> 0x2b8 from mediaanalysisd-service (flags 0x3000, whole surfaces) was
  NOT a rot0 copy but a DOWNSCALE 420f -> 420f on the scale lane (MOD0 0x4444104 = RDMA2|AAL2|RSZ2|TDSHP2|TCC2|WROT2): RDMA pitch 0xc10
  (3088), tile 788x2320 in, RSZ out 512x1514, WROT stride 0x7e0 (2016) -> ~3088x2320 -> 2016x1514, 4 tiles of 512 px out / ~788 px in.
  First try: frame started (mutex sof 1, eof 0), RDMA "data running" (MON1 0x8000), WROT received nothing -> 200 ms timeout (60 =
  ETIMEDOUT).  The abort never polled the WROT soft-reset release: WROT2 stayed at RST_STAT 1, so the next two requests died in the
  compile's reset poll (op 13 = 0x18014 WROT2 RST_STAT want 0; 5 = EIO).  3 failures -> service shutdown (camera too).  Same routing
  as before 0690 (0690 changed only unscaled jobs).  Cause of the stall itself [I]: an unverified combination -- 788-px scale input
  tiles (S2 never ran > 512) and/or scaled NV12 destination (never run by any boot job) and/or 2320 rows.
- piece-0691 (on 0690; nord2_mdp.inc, nord2_mdp_api.h, sweet_m2scaler.inc): vendor-style recovery in every abort (RDMA reset/MON1,
  WROT SOFT_RST 1 -> stat 1 -> 0 -> stat 0, TDSHP 0/2/0; if not back: MDPSYS SW0_RST_B 0x700 pulse for the lane + MOUT reset 0xf00,
  = mt6893/mdp.c cmdqMdpResetEng / cmdq_mdp_reset_with_mmsys; still stuck -> lane dead for the boot, dual pipe / scaling off); a job
  whose reset poll failed is retried once after recovery; scaled requests: NV12 destination refused (ENOTSUP, caller falls back),
  input tiles split to <= 512 px, frames > 1024x512 need the new S2 job scbig (1024x1024 NV12 -> 640x640 BGRA, 3 tiles) =
  N2MDP_CAP_SCALE_BIG (caps 0xffff when all pass), any scaled failure -> scaling off for the boot (kern.n2mdp_scale_off); service:
  scaled failures do not count toward the automatic shutdown.  Camera rotation path unchanged.

## 2026-11-15 ~19:55 GPU fault 'MMU fault on an AS no context holds' + flashing display (q10jfinal19, uptime 550 s) -> 0750 / q10jfinal21 (host only)
Evidence [V-log gf.log 7283-7330, 8670-8720]: right after an edge swipe (TrollStore Helper foreground) 'GPU AS ... mmu_faults=1 orphan=0',
  then the orphan note, then GDVFS VOLT fallback (uv_failed=1); 1294 x '|backboardd| MESA: error: panfrost_batch_submit failed: 5' (lines
  7315-8668 + later bursts); backboardd NEVER appears in 'GPUPROF CTX' again (last at 8705) while 'FB CLIENT backboardd shown=366 fresh=366'
  kept presenting -> buffers never rendered by the GPU shown in rotation = the flashing.  evict=0, binds 11 unchanged, open 9, resets=0,
  flushfail=0, bindfail=0.
Root cause [V-code nord2_gpu_core.c handle_mmu_irqs / n2c_submit, V-log]: fault 1 = a real translation fault in backboardd's OWN AS
  (attributed, no note): context -> N2C_CTX_FAULTED, AS disabled but still held, and FAULTED was PERMANENT (every submit N2C_E_STATE =
  EIO until close; backboardd never closes) = dead compositor.  The 'orphan' was the trailing report of the same stalled access (other
  slot) on the disabled AS still held by the faulted context -- miscounted as orphan (same pattern as perf2a 2026-11-15 02:00).  NOT a
  teardown/eviction race (no eviction, no bind, no close).  The faulting address was never logged (kernel kept it only for the ioctl).
  Voltage: the 10 s uv watchdog is re-armed at EVERY downward OPP step (Nord2GPU.cpp gdvfsSwitch 'lower after the clock'), so it is
  armed almost always under load and blames any software fault; the 662.5 mV step can be neither confirmed nor excluded from this log
  [I: software more likely: same signature came from a userland heap bug before, 654 MHz@662.5 mV ran many boots fault-free, hot SoC].
  After uv_failed=1 the boot runs at 750 mV: a recurrence there excludes the voltage.
Fix 0750 (gpufault-20261115/piece-0750, patch sha256 6571d347...): (1) 'NORD2 GPU FAULT:' line per fault (class context-killed / trailing /
  orphan, AS, owner process, decoded AS_FAULTSTATUS, address vs the client's buffers: INSIDE / guard page / UNMAPPED N ms ago (64-entry
  freed ring) / nearest below, the client's job kind/slot/head, gdvfs kHz + vgpu); (2) trailing reports counted as 'trail', not orphan;
  (3) revival: a FAULTED dynamic client becomes OPEN again (AS handed back, rebound at its next job) once nothing of it is queued (prep
  included) or on the hardware, one clean poll and 20 ms passed; max 3 per 30 s then waits for the window; kill switch kern.n2gfrev /
  boot-arg n2gfrev=0; (4) AS line + trail/revived/revive_held/faulted_refused; GDVFS VOLT prints which counter triggered.  Recovery after a
  fault was: no reset, no resubmit (the faulting batch is lost, mesa logs EIO); now the same plus revival.
